pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo.explain: sim_demo is the part of the ASTRA simulator that people WATCH and that grades each simulated mission. It holds five programs (ros2 run sim_demo ...): demo_panel (the dark Qt window 'ASTRA Simulation - Search Demo' with the live camera, newest photo with detector boxes, detection list, mission phase strip and big buttons), truth_detector (an optional stand-in for the team's AI detector that 'finds' the hiker and tent from the world's answer key), demo_markers (RViz drawings of the search area, targets, photo footprints, detections, route, track and drops), score_run (writes the report card score_report.md/.json and mission_map.png after landing) and pov_server (the live camera as an MJPEG web stream on http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg for Mission Planner). Most of the math lives in ROS-free modules (geo, camera_model, photos, world_info, mission_file, detections, phases, pose_history, zoom, photo_info, photo_geometry, truth_model, scoring, payloads, mission_map, mission_control, mission_planner, run_reset) so it can be tested with plain pytest.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo.how_it_fits: It sits beside the team stack and never changes it. It mostly LISTENS to the same ROS 2 topics the team code uses (/image_detection from new_od, /mavros/state, /mavros/global_position/*, /mavros/mission/reached and /waypoints, /mavros/statustext/recv and /send, /camera/status, /camera/command) and to simulator-only topics (/sim/camera/image, /sim/camera/photo_info, /sim/camera/emulator_state, Gazebo /sim/payload/{person,tent}/odometry). It reads the team photo folder <ros2_ws>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos and sim_worlds' config, truth and mission files. The panel's buttons talk like a pilot: /camera/trigger and /camera/command to video_cam, MAVLink to MAVProxy's extra output udp:127.0.0.1:14553 (or MAVROS services as a fallback) to upload/arm/AUTO/RTL, Windows tasklist.exe/taskkill.exe to open or close Mission Planner, and start_over.sh/run_reset.py for START OVER. truth_detector, when chosen with detector:=truth, publishes the same interfaces/ImageResult on /image_detection as new_od so main_controller cannot tell the difference. Started by sim_bringup's sim.launch.py (which demo.sh and start_sim.sh run): panel, markers, scorer and the optional stand-in through launch/demo_nodes.launch.py, pov_server directly; with demo.sh, score_run writes into the run folder ~/.astra_sim/runs/<time>_<world>/. run_reset.py (START OVER) restarts the per-run helpers between flights.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/laun.explain: A ROS 2 launch file that starts the demo tools in one go: demo_panel (if panel:=true), demo_markers (if markers:=true), score_run (if score:=true) and truth_detector ONLY when detector:=truth. mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/laun.how_it_fits: Included by sim_bringup's full simulator launch and usable alone next to a running simulation: 'ros2 launch sim_demo demo_nodes.launch.py world:=runway detector:=truth'. It does not start pov_server (sim.launch.py does that).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/launc.explain: Builds the launch plan: one DeclareLaunchArgument per entry of the ARGS table, then four Node actions. Every node gets world, worlds_dir, photo_dir and use_sim_time; the panel also gets detector, mavlink_url, mission_link and auto_start; the markers get frame_id; the truth_detector gets geolocation and only starts when the detector argument equals 'truth' (a PythonExpression); score_run gets run_dir and detector.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/launc.called_when: Automatically by 'ros2 launch' when this file is launched or included.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/launc.effects: Starts up to four processes (demo_panel, demo_markers, truth_detector, score_run) with output to the screen.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Marks the sim_demo folder as a Python package and sets __version__ = '0.1.0'. Its docstring says the pure-math modules do not need ROS, so they can be tested anywhere with plain pytest.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Lets other code write 'from sim_demo import geo' or 'python3 -m sim_demo.mission_planner'.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: The map math of the demo tools. It turns GPS latitude/longitude (degrees) into metres east, north and up of the simulator's home point and back, measures distances, parses the 'lat,lon,alt,heading' home string and converts between compass headings and math angles. It knows two ways to flatten the Earth: 'ardupilot' (the default: the exact formulas ArduPilot SITL uses to make the drone's simulated GPS, a sphere of radius 6378100 m) and 'wgs84' (the real Earth ellipsoid); they differ by up to about 1 m inside a SUAS field.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python, no ROS. Every tool that compares a GPS position (MAVROS /mavros/global_position/global, the GPS in photo file names, the team's aim and drop waypoints) with a Gazebo position (truth targets, payload landing points, RViz markers) goes through GeoOrigin: world_info, pose_history, photo_info, photo_geometry, truth_model, truth_detector, demo_markers, scoring, score_run, mission_file. This works because the Gazebo world's <spherical_coordinates> origin is the same point as the SITL --home, so 'metres from home' ARE Gazebo world coordinates (x east, y north, z up).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Returns how much shorter one degree of longitude is than one degree of latitude at a given latitude, exactly like ArduPilot's Location::longitude_scale(): cos(latitude), but never below 0.01 so nothing ever divides by zero.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Inside GeoOrigin.to_enu and GeoOrigin.to_geo in the default 'ardupilot' convention.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Computes the real Earth's two curvature radii (WGS-84 ellipsoid, equator radius 6378137 m) at a latitude: the north-south radius (metres per radian of latitude) and the east-west radius (times cos(latitude) gives metres per radian of longitude).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Only in the 'wgs84' convention of GeoOrigin.to_enu / to_geo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: A small frozen record of the GPS point that is (0, 0, 0) in the Gazebo world, which is the SITL home: lat, lon, alt (metres above sea level, default 0) and convention ('ardupilot' by default, or 'wgs84'). Its two methods turn GPS into metres around that point and back.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.how_it_fits: Built from the world config's home string by world_info and handed to almost every other module.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Converts a GPS point into metres east, north and up of the origin. In the default 'ardupilot' mode, north = latitude difference x 111318.845 m per degree, the longitude difference is wrapped to -180..180 and shrunk by cos of the middle latitude; in 'wgs84' mode it uses the ellipsoid radii. Up is the altitude minus the origin's altitude (0 when no altitude is given).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.inputs: lat, lon in degrees; optional alt in metres above sea level.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The reverse of to_enu: turns metres east, north and up of the origin back into latitude, longitude and altitude, with the same formulas as the chosen convention.
Great-circle distance in metres between two GPS points on a round Earth of radius 6371008.8 m (good to about 0.3 %).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Only by the unit tests (test_geo.py) at the time of reading; the tools use local_distance_m instead.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Distance in metres between two GPS points measured on the flat map around a GeoOrigin: both points go through origin.to_enu and the straight-line east/north distance is returned. For the short distances of a SUAS field this matches what the simulator's own GPS math gives.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By pose_history when it looks for the recorded drone position nearest to a photo's file-name GPS.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Reads the home string of a world config, written like SITL's --home option: 'lat,lon,alt_msl,heading_deg' (for example '36.2143000,-96.0068000,210.0,0'). Missing trailing numbers become 0 and spaces are ignored; it raises ValueError when latitude or longitude is missing or not a number.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By world_info when it loads sim_worlds/config/<world>.yaml.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Turns a compass heading (0 = north, turning clockwise) into a math/ENU yaw angle (0 = east, turning counter-clockwise): yaw = 90 - heading, wrapped to -180..180 degrees.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Only by the unit tests at the time of reading.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The opposite of compass_to_enu_yaw_deg: turns an ENU yaw (0 = east, counter-clockwise) into a compass heading (0 = north, clockwise) in 0..360 degrees.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By ros_common's FlightData when it gets the drone's heading from /mavros/local_position/pose (a quaternion) because no compass heading arrived.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Wraps any angle into the range above -180 and up to 180 degrees (for example 190 becomes -170).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By compass_to_enu_yaw_deg.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Wraps any angle into the range 0 (included) to 360 (not included) degrees (for example -10 becomes 350).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By enu_yaw_to_compass_deg and by pose_history when it stores headings.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Takes a rotation written as a quaternion (x, y, z, w) and returns only its turn around the vertical axis (yaw) in degrees, counter-clockwise from east (ENU).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By ros_common's FlightData on /mavros/local_position/pose messages (heading fallback).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: The camera math of the simulated SIYI camera (a pinhole camera with square pixels). It answers three questions: where a point in the world shows up in a photo (which pixel), which patch of ground a photo covers (its 'footprint', 4 corners), and where an object's 3D box lands in the picture. Conventions: world = Gazebo ENU metres; camera yaw = compass heading of the image top, pitch 0 = horizon and -90 = straight down (SIYI sign); pixels like OpenCV with (0, 0) at the top-left; zoom narrows the view with tan(hfov_zoomed/2) = tan(hfov/2) / zoom. Default field of view 1.4137 rad (81 deg); profiles zr10 2560x1440, a8mini 3840x2160, video 1280x720.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python, no ROS. truth_model uses it to decide which targets a photo shows and to draw their boxes, photo_geometry/photo_info build camera poses with it, demo_markers and mission_map draw photo footprints, scoring checks which targets lay inside each footprint, and truth_detector projects box centres to the ground in geolocation:=projected mode.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: A frozen record of the picture's size and lens: width and height in pixels, hfov_rad (horizontal field of view at zoom 1, default 1.4137 rad = 81 deg) and zoom (1.0 = widest). Its properties work out the zoomed field of view, the focal length in pixels and the image centre.

Makes a CameraIntrinsics from a profile name: 'zr10' (2560x1440, the default photo size), 'a8mini' (3840x2160) or 'video' (1280x720), with an optional zoom and field of view. An unknown name raises KeyError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Only by the unit tests at the time of reading.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The horizontal field of view after zoom, in radians: 2 x atan(tan(hfov/2) / zoom). At zoom 1 it is just hfov; at zoom 5 the view is about 5 times narrower.
Focal length in pixels: (width / 2) / tan(effective_hfov / 2). It says how many pixels one unit of sideways offset at distance one becomes.
Focal length in pixels along the image's y axis; equal to fx because the pixels are square.
The x pixel of the image centre (width / 2).
The y pixel of the image centre (height / 2).
The vertical field of view after zoom, in radians, worked out from the height and fy. Nothing in the repo used it at the time of reading.

A frozen record of where the camera is and where it looks: east, north, up (metres in the Gazebo world), yaw_deg (compass heading of the image top), pitch_deg (default -90 = straight down) and roll_deg. Optional 'axes' gives the camera's three direction vectors directly (for example from the emulator's optical quaternion) and then wins over the angles, which are ambiguous when looking straight down.

Turns the camera emulator's optical-frame quaternion ('optical_quat_xyzw': x right, y down, z forward) into three unit vectors in world ENU: image-right, image-down and the viewing direction (the columns of the rotation matrix). It normalises the quaternion first.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By photo_info when it builds a camera pose from an emulator photo record.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Dot product of two 3D vectors (a.x*b.x + a.y*b.y + a.z*b.z). Small helper for project_point.
Cross product of two 3D vectors (a vector at right angles to both). Small helper for camera_axes.

Returns the camera's three unit direction vectors in world ENU: image-right, image-down and the optical axis (where the camera looks). If the pose carries 'axes' it returns those; otherwise it builds them from yaw (heading of the image top) and pitch (tilt), then turns the picture about the optical axis by roll (positive = the right side of the picture goes down).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By project_point and pixel_ray (and by the fake-mission test renderer).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Finds the pixel (u, v) where a world point (east, north, up) appears in the picture using the pinhole formula u = fx * right/forward + cx, v = fy * down/forward + cy. The pixel may lie outside the picture; returns None when the point is behind the camera.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By project_box for each of an object's 8 box corners.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The reverse direction of project_point: gives the world direction (not normalised) of the line of sight through pixel (u, v).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By pixel_to_ground.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Finds the spot on flat ground (height ground_up, default 0) that pixel (u, v) looks at, by following the pixel's line of sight down until it hits the ground. Returns (east, north) in metres, or None when the pixel looks at the sky or farther away than max_range (default 2000 m).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By footprint for the 4 photo corners, and by truth_detector in geolocation:=projected mode for a box centre.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Works out the patch of flat ground a photo covers: the ground points under the 4 image corners in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. Returns None if any corner looks above the horizon (a tilted photo with an endless footprint).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By photo_geometry (and through it demo_markers, score_run and mission_map) for every photo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Answers 'is point (x, y) inside this polygon?' with the ray-casting rule (count how many edges a line to the right crosses; odd = inside).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By scoring to test whether a true target lies inside a photo footprint or a search area.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Area of a simple polygon with the shoelace formula (square metres for ground points, square pixels for pixel points).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Only by the unit tests at the time of reading.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: How many metres of ground one pixel covers at the centre of a straight-down photo: height above ground / fx.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Only by the unit tests at the time of reading.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Returns the 8 corners of an object's box (length along its own x axis, width along its y axis, height up) standing on the ground at (east, north, up) and turned by yaw_deg (ENU: 0 = east, counter-clockwise).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By truth_model for each true target (and distractor) before projecting it into a photo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: A frozen record of where an object's box falls in a picture: x1, y1, x2, y2 = the part INSIDE the picture (pixels), visible_fraction = how much of the full box is inside (0..1), full_width/full_height = the uncut box size in pixels, and center_norm = how far the visible box centre is from the picture centre (0 = centre, 1 = a corner).
Centre x pixel of the visible part of the box.
Centre y pixel of the visible part of the box.
Width in pixels of the visible part of the box (x2 - x1).
Height in pixels of the visible part of the box (y2 - y1).
The longest side of the FULL (uncut) box in pixels, which says how big the object looks in the photo.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By truth_model: targets shorter than min_pixels (12 px) are not detected, and confidence grows towards good_pixels (60 px).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Projects an object's 8 box corners into the picture, takes the smallest rectangle around them, cuts it to the picture's edges and measures how much of it is visible and how far from the centre it is. Returns a ProjectedBox, or None when any corner is behind the camera or nothing lands inside the picture.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By truth_model for each true target in each photo.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Everything about the team's photo folder: where it is, how photos are named and how to notice new ones. It copies the team's own rules: video_cam saves every photo into <ros2_ws>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos/ with the drone's GPS in the name ('<lat:.6f> , <lon:.6f>.jpg', note the spaces around the comma), writes '<name>.tmp.jpg' first and renames it when finished, and detection/geotag.py reads the GPS back the same way parse_latlon_from_name does.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python, no ROS. demo_panel, truth_detector, demo_markers and score_run all call resolve_photo_dir to find the SAME folder the team's camera node writes to and new_od reads, then use PhotoWatcher to see each finished photo exactly once.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Reads the GPS position back out of a photo file name like '36.214300 , -96.006800.jpg'. It drops the folder and extension, splits at ' , ' and turns both halves into numbers; names without that delimiter or with non-numbers (for example 'IMG_0042.jpg') give (None, None). Same rules as the team's detection/geotag.py.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By PhotoWatcher.poll for every new photo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Builds the file name video_cam gives a photo taken at (lat, lon): f'{lat:.6f} , {lon:.6f}.jpg'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the tests and the fake-mission test, which write photos the way video_cam does.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Says whether a file name is a finished photo: it must end in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .bmp (same list as new_od and main_controller), must not contain '.tmp.' (a half-written file) and must not start with a dot (a hidden file).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By list_photos and PhotoWatcher.poll.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Walks up from a file or folder, at most 10 levels, to the first folder that has BOTH an install/ and a src/ folder (a colcon workspace) and returns '<workspace>/src'. It is the same search video_cam's get_ros2_ws_directory() does, so it lands on the same workspace as the camera node. Returns None when no workspace is found.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By resolve_photo_dir.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Finds the team's photo folder, trying in order: 1) the photo_dir parameter, 2) the ASTRA_PHOTO_DIR environment variable, 3) the workspace of the installed video_cam package (the camera's own rule), 4) the Linux-side repo copy ($ASTRA_REPO, else ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026), 5) the workspace holding sim_demo itself, 6) video_cam's fallback ~/video_cam/mapping_photos. The folder may not exist yet (the camera node makes it at its first photo).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Once at start-up of demo_panel, truth_detector, demo_markers and score_run.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.outputs: (folder_path, a short text saying which rule found it); the panel shows that text so a wrong folder is easy to spot.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Lists every finished photo in a folder, oldest first, as (modification time, full path). Returns an empty list when the folder does not exist or cannot be read.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the demo panel window at start, to list (and count) the photos already in the folder before this run.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: A record for one new, completely written photo: full path, file name, modification time, lat/lon from the name (None if none), size in bytes, and preexisting = True when the photo was already in the folder when watching started.

Notices new photos in a folder by looking at it again and again (polling; no inotify needed, so it works on every system). A photo is reported once, when it is at least min_age_s (0.3 s) old and its size did not change between two looks, which means it is fully written (the same idea as new_od's _is_file_ready()).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.how_it_fits: Each of the four nodes owns one watcher on the team photo folder and calls poll() from a timer.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Remembers the folder to watch (it may not exist yet), the minimum age (default 0.3 s) and whether photos already in the folder at the first look should be reported (default yes, flagged preexisting), and starts with empty size and 'already reported' lists.

Looks at the folder once and returns the photos that became ready since the last look, oldest first. On the very first look every existing photo is marked as seen (and returned as preexisting if report_existing is on); later a photo is returned when its size stayed the same since the previous look and it is old enough. Files that disappeared are forgotten, so a new file with the same name is reported again.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: From a timer in each node (truth_detector every poll_period_s = 0.5 s).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: How many photos the watcher has reported so far, including the preexisting ones. No caller used it at the time of reading.

Gets a picture's width and height without decoding all its pixels. It uses Pillow when installed; otherwise it reads up to 256 KB of the file and walks the JPEG header markers until it finds the frame header (SOF) that holds the size. Returns None when the file cannot be read.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By photo_geometry to know a photo's real resolution (2560x1440 or 3840x2160) before building the camera model.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Reads an ArduPilot mission file ('.waypoints', the 'QGC WPL 110' text format of Mission Planner and MAVProxy: one tab-separated line per item, line 0 = home) and works out its structure: takeoff item, the first DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL (where photos start), the waypoints that make the search lanes, the hold point and the RETURN_TO_LAUNCH. Its index rules copy the team code so the panel agrees with it: waypoint_manager's takeoff_index / rtl_index / last_before_rtl = rtl - 1 / buffer_wp = rtl - 2, and main_controller's 'last NAV command (16..22) before RTL'.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python, no ROS. demo_panel uses it to upload the mission and to say 'Searching: lane 2 of 3'; phases uses the MissionSummary; demo_markers draws the route and a search box from it; score_run uses it for the report.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: One line of a .waypoints file, which is one MAVLink MISSION_ITEM: seq, current, frame, command (MAV_CMD number such as 16 WAYPOINT, 22 TAKEOFF, 20 RETURN_TO_LAUNCH, 203 DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL), param1..param4, lat, lon, alt and autocontinue.
A readable name for the item's command, for example 'WAYPOINT' for 16 or 'DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL' for 203; unknown numbers become 'CMD_<number>'.

The structure of a survey mission as mission index numbers (-1 = not there): takeoff_index, rtl_index, last_before_rtl, buffer_wp (as waypoint_manager computes them), last_nav_before_rtl (main_controller's hold trigger), digicam_index (first DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL), hold_index, the survey waypoint list in flight order, the lanes as (start, end) pairs and survey_alt (the middle altitude of the survey waypoints).
How many search lanes the mission has.

Tells which lane (counting from 1) the drone is flying after it reached mission item reached_seq: it counts the survey waypoints already passed, two per lane. Before the first survey waypoint it answers lane 1, after the last one it stays on the last lane, and with no lanes it answers 0.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By phases when /mavros/mission/reached arrives, to write 'Searching: lane i of n'.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Turns the text of a QGC WPL 110 file into a list of MissionItem. It skips empty lines and '#' comments, insists that the first line starts with 'QGC WPL', and needs 12 fields per line; otherwise it raises ValueError naming the bad line.
Opens a .waypoints file (UTF-8) and parses it with parse_waypoints_text.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: At start-up of demo_panel, demo_markers and score_run for the world's mission (sim_worlds/missions/<world>_survey.waypoints).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Works out a MissionSummary from the list of command numbers (list position = mission index). It finds TAKEOFF (22), RETURN_TO_LAUNCH (20, giving last_before_rtl and buffer_wp) and the first DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL (203); the waypoint just before the camera item is the start of lane 1 (ArduPilot runs a DO item while it flies the NEXT leg), and the waypoints after it pair up as lane end / next lane start. The hold waypoint is cut off the end: given by hold_index (the config's survey.planned.hold_wp), or else an odd leftover waypoint. survey_alt is the middle value of the survey altitudes.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Through analyze_items, and directly by the demo panel when the autopilot's own mission arrives on /mavros/mission/waypoints.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Runs analyze() on parsed MissionItems: it passes each item's command and altitude, using the item's position in the list as its index.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By demo_panel, demo_markers and score_run after loading the mission file.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Draws a rectangle (east, north in metres, 4 corners) around the survey waypoints, skipping items at (0, 0). Returns [] when there are fewer than 2 points or the rectangle would be flat.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By demo_markers as the 'search area' outline when the world's truth file has none.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Reads a simulated world's description: the world config sim_worlds/config/<world>.yaml (home GPS point, spawn, mission file, truth file, survey hints) and the answer key sim_worlds/truth/<world>.yaml (where the hiker and tent really are, the search areas, the distractors). It is forgiving on purpose: targets may be written in GPS degrees or Gazebo metres, listed or keyed by name, with the class under many key names; anything it cannot understand is skipped with a warning instead of crashing. Everything becomes the person or tent class, because the team's detector only reports class_id '0' person and '1' tent.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python (needs PyYAML). Its load_world() result (a WorldInfo with origin, targets with both lat/lon and east/north, search area polygons) feeds demo_panel, truth_detector, demo_markers, score_run and the tests.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: One real target from the answer key: name (for example 'hiker'), cls ('person' or 'tent'), lat/lon in degrees, east/north/up in Gazebo metres (the bottom centre of its box), yaw_deg, size (length, width, height in metres) and posture ('lying', 'sitting' or 'standing' for persons, '' otherwise). Distractors (look-alikes) use the same record.

Everything sim_demo knows about one world: its name, the GPS origin (= SITL home), home heading, the true targets, the first search area and all search areas as (name, polygon in metres), paths of the mission, truth, world and config files, the spawn pose, survey hints from the config (survey.planned, e.g. hold_wp), the distractors and a list of warnings found while loading.
The mission index of the hold waypoint taken from the config's survey.planned.hold_wp, or -1 if it is missing or not a number.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By demo_panel and demo_markers when they analyse the mission.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Turns any class word into 'person' or 'tent': mannequin, manikin, hiker, human, dummy and people become 'person'; tent and shelter become 'tent'. It first tries an exact match, then whether one of those words appears inside the text; anything else gives None.

Finds the folder with sim_worlds' files (config/, truth/, missions/, worlds/): the worlds_dir parameter if set, else the ASTRA_WORLDS_DIR environment variable, else the installed sim_worlds share folder from ament_index; '' if none is found.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By load_world when the world is given by name.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Opens a YAML file and reads it safely with yaml.safe_load (PyYAML is imported only here).

Small helper: returns the value of the first key from a list of possible key names that exists in a dict and is not None, else a default. This is how the loader accepts 'lat' or 'latitude', 'class' or 'type', and so on.
Turns [1, 2], (1, 2), '1, 2' or '1 2' into a list of floats [1.0, 2.0]; returns None if the value is not a list of numbers.
Guesses whether a pair of numbers is GPS (lat, lon): true when both are within 1 degree of the world origin's latitude and longitude, otherwise they are taken as metres.

Turns one point written in any accepted style into (east, north) metres: a dict with lat/lon (converted with the origin) or x/y, or a list/string of two numbers that are treated as GPS or metres (by geo_hint, or else by _looks_geo). Returns None if it cannot understand it.

Reads a polygon written as a list of points or as a dict. For sim_worlds' search areas it prefers corners_xy / corners_enu (metres) over corners_latlon (GPS); a {center, size, yaw} rectangle is turned into its 4 corners (yaw in radians unless yaw_deg is given); keys like latlon, gps, xy, points, polygon or vertices are also accepted. Returns (east, north) points, or [] when there are fewer than 3 understandable points.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By parse_search_areas.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Gets a target's yaw in degrees from whichever key it has: yaw_deg, heading_deg, yaw_rad, yaw (taken as radians when it is small enough to be radians), or the 6th number of an SDF-style 'x y z roll pitch yaw' pose; 0 when none.

Turns one answer-key entry into a TruthTarget. It finds the name, the class (from many possible keys, or from the name itself), the posture (lying by default for persons), the position from lat/lon or x/y or a position/xyz/pose value (filling in whichever of GPS or metres is missing), the size (or a default: lying person 1.8 x 0.5 x 0.3 m, tent 2.4 x 2.1 x 1.4 m) and the bounding-box centre that sim_worlds writes separately (center, center_z: the box bottom is center_z minus half the height).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.outputs: (TruthTarget or None, a problem text explaining why it was skipped).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Reads a whole truth document: the target list from a 'targets', 'objects', 'ground_truth', 'truth', 'items' or 'odlc' key (or a document keyed by target names), each turned into a TruthTarget with parse_target, plus the first search area. Every skipped entry adds a warning, and 'no person/tent targets found' is added if nothing was usable.

Returns all search areas of a truth or config document as (name, polygon in metres): sim_worlds' 'search_areas' list, or else a single polygon under search_area, search_area_polygon, search_polygon, search_zone, search_boundary or area.
Turns a path from the config into an absolute path: '~' is expanded and a relative path is joined to the sim_worlds folder; an empty path stays ''.

Loads a world by name (for example 'runway') or by the path of a config YAML. It reads the config, builds the GeoOrigin from 'home' (a 'lat,lon,alt,heading' string or a dict), resolves the mission, truth and world file paths, keeps spawn and survey.planned, then reads the truth file (targets, search areas, and distractors that a detector could call person/tent). A broken or missing truth file only adds a warning so the panel still opens; a missing config raises FileNotFoundError and a config without home raises ValueError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: At start-up of demo_panel, truth_detector, demo_markers and score_run (and by the tests' conftest).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.inputs: world name or config path, worlds_dir ('' = find it), truth_override ('' = the config's truth file).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Turns the team detector's output message (interfaces/msg/ImageResult on /image_detection, RELIABLE depth 10) into simple Python records, builds that same message for the truth_detector stand-in, and repeats main_controller's choice of target. In the message, bbox.center.position.x/y is the box centre in photo pixels, results[0].hypothesis.class_id is '0' person or '1' tent with its score, and latitude/longitude are the drone GPS parsed from the photo's file name.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python (ROS message classes are imported only when a message is built). demo_panel, demo_markers and score_run read every /image_detection message through image_result_to_frame; truth_detector publishes through frame_to_image_result; best_per_class is how the panel, markers and scorer show 'what main_controller will fly to'.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: One detection box in photo pixels: cls ('person', 'tent' or 'class <id>' for an unknown id), score (confidence 0..1), and the box centre cx, cy and size w, h in pixels of the full-resolution photo.
The box as its corners (x1, y1, x2, y2) in pixels, worked out from the centre and size.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By panel_widgets when it draws the box on the photo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Everything one ImageResult message says about one photo: image_name (the photo file name), lat/lon from the message (0.0 if the name had no GPS), the person/tent boxes, the detector's method text, num_detections, the classes and confidences lists, waypoint_index, the time this program received it, the header stamp and saved_to (the annotated picture's path).
True when the message came from the truth_detector stand-in instead of the AI model: its method text starts with 'truth_detector'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel (DETECTOR pill REAL / STAND-IN and the amber banner) and by score_run (the report says which detector ran).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: False when the detector found no GPS in the file name, which shows up as lat = lon = 0.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By demo_markers, the panel, score_run and scoring before they use the message's position.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Converts one ImageResult message (or any object with the same fields) into a DetectionFrame. For every detection it reads the box centre (also the old vision_msgs center.x/center.y layout), size, class_id ('0' -> person, '1' -> tent) and score; missing or odd fields become defaults instead of errors.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: In the /image_detection callback of demo_panel, demo_markers and score_run.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.inputs: msg: the ImageResult; received: arrival time (default now).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Builds an interfaces/msg/ImageResult from a DetectionFrame, filled exactly like the team's new_od does: header frame_id 'camera', image_name, an ISO timestamp, method, slice_size, overlap, waypoint_index, latitude/longitude, a vision_msgs Detection2DArray with only person/tent boxes (class_id '0' / '1' and score), empty masks, and the parallel classes / confidences / areas / descriptions lists. The message classes are imported inside the function so the module works without ROS (the tests pass fake classes in).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By truth_detector for every photo it reports.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.outputs: An ImageResult ready to publish on /image_detection.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Repeats how the team's main_controller.image_result_cb picks its targets: going through the frames in arrival order, for each class (person, tent) it keeps the single box with the highest score, and a new box only wins when its score is STRICTLY greater.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel ('what main_controller will fly to'), demo_markers (the 'best' layer) and score_run / scoring (what was chosen).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.outputs: {'person': (score, frame, box), 'tent': (...)} for the classes seen.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: A state machine that works out which phase the mission is in: Waiting > Taking off > Searching (lane i of n) > Processing photos > Flying to target > Dropping > Returning > Landed. It uses only messages the real flight stack already sends: /mavros/state (armed, mode), /mavros/global_position/rel_alt, /mavros/mission/reached, the autopilot's STATUSTEXT ('Mission: 3 DigiCamCtrl') and the team nodes' STATUSTEXT ('Reached last WP. Holding ...', 'Targets: tent@11 -> person@12. Diverting.', 'Resumed AUTO -> WP 11', 'Over tent: loiter 6s then drop', 'Servo 13 -> 1400', 'RTL', 'Camera trigger STARTED', 'Captured ... image #N', 'Zoom set to Xx'). It has no ROS imports: feed it plain values and read phase, detail and events.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: The panel's phase strip, demo_markers (drop events) and score_run's time line all run one PhaseTracker. The texts it parses are the ones AGENTS.md tells teammates never to change in main_controller, mapping and video_cam. sim_bringup's phase_monitor does a similar job for demo.sh.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: One thing worth putting on the time line: time t, a kind ('phase', 'drop', 'release_closed', 'over', 'targets', 'detected', 'photo', 'armed', 'disarmed', 'mode', 'zoom') and a data dict (for a drop: cls, channel, pwm).

The phase state machine. Feed it messages with on_state, on_rel_alt, on_reached and on_statustext (and the mission with set_mission); read phase (one of the 8 phase names), detail (a sentence like 'lane 2 of 3'), events and history. It also remembers the target plan from main_controller, which payloads were released, how many photos were captured, the detected classes and the camera zoom.

Starts in the Waiting phase ('waiting for the autopilot') with empty lists and the servo-to-payload map (default: servo 11 and 9 = person, 13 and 14 = tent, matching main_controller's PERSON_SERVO_CHANNELS [11] and TENT_SERVO_CHANNELS [13]).

ArduPilot prints 'Mission: N RTL' the moment it starts the mission's RTL item, which is about a second BEFORE main_controller takes over in GUIDED. So an RTL text is only believed if the drone is still in AUTO RTL_GRACE_S (4 s) later; then the phase becomes Returning ('flying home (mission RTL)'). If the mode changed meanwhile, the pending RTL is forgotten.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: At the start of every on_* input method.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The position of the current phase in the PHASES list (0 = Waiting, 7 = Landed).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel to light the phase strip box and tick the earlier ones.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Only the phase-change events, oldest first.
The time (seconds) at which the current phase began; 0.0 while still in the first Waiting phase.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel for '(for 1:21)' after the phase detail.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Moves to a phase with a detail sentence. When the phase really changes it records the start time and adds a 'phase' event; when it is the same phase only the detail sentence is updated.

Writes the detail sentence for the Searching phase: 'flying to the search area (3 lanes)' before the first survey waypoint, 'lane 2 of 3' while on the lanes, or 'past waypoint N' / 'flying the search pattern' when the mission structure is unknown.
True while the phase is one of Taking off, Searching, Processing photos, Flying to target, Dropping or Returning.
Gives the tracker the mission structure (a MissionSummary with lanes, takeoff and hold items) and refreshes the lane sentence if it is already searching.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel and score_run after loading the world's mission file, and again by the panel when the autopilot's mission arrives.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Feeds one /mavros/state message (connected, armed, mode). It logs armed/disarmed/mode events; arming from Waiting or Landed starts Taking off (after a landing, the new flight first clears the old drops and target plan); RTL or LAND mode in flight means Returning; AUTO during Dropping with targets left means Flying to target (main_controller goes back to AUTO after a drop); disarming after the drone flew (or climbed above 2 m) means Landed ('mission complete - motors off').

Feeds the height above home from /mavros/global_position/rel_alt. It remembers the highest height, marks 'the drone really flew' once it is above 2 m while armed, and during Taking off writes 'climbing: 12 m of 30 m' (the survey altitude from the mission).

Feeds /mavros/mission/reached (wp_seq). Reaching the takeoff item (or later) while taking off starts Searching; while searching it updates the lane sentence (or 'end of the search pattern' at main_controller's hold item); while flying to targets, reaching a target's waypoint from the plan means Dropping ('over the tent: loiter, then release').

Feeds one STATUSTEXT from /mavros/statustext/recv (autopilot) or /send (team nodes) and moves the phase with regular expressions: 'Mission: N Takeoff/DigiCam/WP/RTL/Land', 'Camera trigger STARTED' -> Searching, 'Holding to finish image processing' / 'Reached last WP' -> Processing photos (max 90 s), 'No valid targets' -> Returning, 'Targets: tent@11 -> person@12. Diverting.' -> stores the plan and Flying to target, 'Resumed AUTO -> WP N', 'Over tent' -> Dropping, 'Servo 13 -> 1400' (1000 us or more = open) -> a drop event for that payload, 'RTL' -> Returning. It also counts 'Captured <res> image #N', notes 'Detected <class>' and 'Zoom set to Xx'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: For every STATUSTEXT the panel, demo_markers and score_run receive (via ros_common's FlightData).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Remembers where the drone was during the last minutes (up to 30 minutes, 50000 samples) so that when a photo file appears, seconds after the shutter fired, the tools can find where the drone was, how high it flew and which way it pointed AT THE MOMENT THE PHOTO WAS TAKEN. Trick: video_cam names each photo after the latest /mavros/global_position/global fix, which is recorded here too, so the recorded sample whose position equals the name's position IS the shutter moment. All times are wall-clock seconds (time.time()), the same clock as file modification times.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python. ros_common's FlightData fills one PoseHistory from MAVROS; photo_geometry asks it for each photo's capture pose (the fallback when the camera emulator's record is missing), and demo_markers / score_run use it for the drone track and drop positions.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The drone's state at one moment: wall-clock time t, lat/lon (degrees), alt_msl and rel_alt (height above home = height above ground on flat ground), heading_deg (compass, 0 = north, clockwise) and ground_speed (m/s). Unknown values are NaN.
Straight-line blend between two numbers a and b by fraction f (0 = a, 1 = b); if one of them is unknown (NaN) the other one is used.
Blends two compass headings the short way round (from 350 to 10 degrees passes through 0, not 180), returning 0..360; an unknown (NaN) side is skipped.
A time-ordered list of PoseSamples with lookups by time (at_time), by GPS position (nearest_to) and the photo-specific capture_pose; old samples are thrown away automatically.
Creates an empty history that keeps samples for max_age_s (default 1800 s = 30 min) and at most max_samples (default 50000).
The number of samples stored, so len(history) works.

Adds a sample at its place in time order (a late, out-of-order sample is inserted where it belongs) and, when the list grows too long or too old, deletes the oldest samples beyond max_age_s / max_samples.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By ros_common's FlightData for every MAVROS GPS fix.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The newest sample, or None when nothing has been recorded.

The drone state at time t, blended between the two recorded samples around it (position, heights, speed, and heading the short way round). Returns None when the history is empty or t is more than max_gap_s (default 5 s) away from every sample.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By capture_pose (time-only fallback), demo_markers and score_run (where the drone was when a servo opened).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Finds, among the samples between t_min and t_max, the one closest to a GPS point and returns it with its distance in metres (None, infinity when the window is empty). No caller used it at the time of reading.

Best guess of the drone state when a photo was taken. With GPS in the file name it looks at the samples of the last window_s (60 s) and takes the one nearest to the name's position, if it is within max_match_m (3 m); samples that are almost as near (within 0.3 m, e.g. while hovering) are decided by how close they are to the usual shutter-to-file delay (latency_s, 1 s). That sample is returned with the name's exact lat/lon ('gps-match'). Otherwise it blends the state at file time minus the delay ('time'), or gives up ('none').
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Through FlightData.capture_pose, by photo_geometry for every new photo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: A copy of the samples between t_min and t_max, oldest first (all of them by default).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By score_run's collect(), which turns the samples from 5 s before take-off to 5 s after landing into the drone track (a point every 2 m or more) for run_data.json and mission_map.png.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Keeps track of how far the simulated camera was zoomed in when each photo was taken. This matters: last year's camera code racks the lens to 5x at the start of the search (video_cam CAPTURE_ZOOM_X = 5.0 on 'capture_setup'), and at 5x a photo covers 5 times less ground in each direction. Sources, best first: a fixed zoom parameter (> 0), the camera emulator's own report, the team camera node's text 'Zoom set to 5.0x' or a 'zoom_absolute N' command on /camera/command, else 1.0.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python. ros_common's FlightData owns one ZoomTracker and feeds it; photo_geometry asks zoom_at(capture time) when it has no emulator record for a photo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Remembers zoom values over time from several sources and answers 'what was the zoom at time t, and where did that number come from?'. Source labels: 'parameter', 'camera emulator', 'video_cam status text', '/camera/command', 'default (no zoom reported)'.
Creates empty zoom histories; fixed_zoom > 0 makes every answer that fixed value (for testing; the truth_detector/demo_markers/score_run 'zoom' parameter).
Inserts a (time, value) pair at its place in time order; when a list passes 5000 entries the oldest 1000 are dropped.
Records a zoom value (only if above 0) that the camera emulator reported at time t.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By FlightData when /sim/camera/emulator_state arrives.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Looks for 'Zoom set to <number>x' in a status text (video_cam sends it after it confirmed the zoom) and records that zoom. Returns True when the text carried a zoom.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By FlightData for every STATUSTEXT.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Looks for a 'zoom_absolute <n>' or 'zoom_auto <n>' command on /camera/command and records that zoom. Returns True when it was such a command.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By FlightData for every /camera/command message.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Returns (zoom, source) in effect at time t: the fixed zoom if set; else the latest emulator value at or before t (or its first one); else the latest status/command value before t; else (1.0, 'default (no zoom reported)').
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By photo_geometry for photos without an emulator record.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Uses the camera emulator's exact record of every photo it made (topic /sim/camera/photo_info, a JSON std_msgs/String per photo from siyi_emulator, RELIABLE + TRANSIENT_LOCAL) to know precisely where the camera was and where it pointed for each photo that video_cam later saves in the team folder. The JSON holds wall_time, image size, zoom, hfov_rad, camera_world (position_enu_m, optical_quat_xyzw) and sd_name (IMG_NNNN.jpg). The hard part is pairing records with saved files: video_cam picks the file name from the GPS FIRST and takes the photo later, one at a time, in order.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python. FlightData feeds the records in (add_json); photo_geometry asks match() for each new photo; truth_detector, demo_markers and score_run therefore all use the exact Gazebo camera pose when it is available.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: One photo as the emulator recorded it: wall-clock time t, the SD-card name (IMG_NNNN.jpg), CameraIntrinsics (size, lens field of view, zoom), the exact CameraPose in Gazebo world ENU, and matched = True once it has been paired with a saved file.

Reads one /sim/camera/photo_info JSON text into an EmulatorPhoto: wall_time (ISO, UTC) becomes epoch seconds, image width/height, total zoom, lens field of view (default 1.4137 rad), camera position in metres, the optical quaternion turned into camera axes, compass heading and pitch. Returns None when a needed field is missing or broken.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By PhotoInfoIndex.add_json.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Keeps the emulator's photo records (newest 2000) and pairs each newly saved photo file with the record it came from. Rules, best first: when the moment the drone was at the file name's GPS is known, the FIRST unmatched record made after that moment; otherwise the unmatched record whose camera position is NEAREST to the name's GPS (within 15 m; about equally near ones go oldest first); without GPS, the oldest unmatched record. Older records that were never matched are then marked used too: video_cam saves photos one at a time, in order, so those were never saved. A lock makes it safe across threads.
Stores the world origin and the matching limits: window_s 30 s (a record must be at most this old when the file appears), max_distance_m 15 m, tie_tolerance_m 2 m; starts with no records and a lock.
Parses one /sim/camera/photo_info message and stores it in time order (deleting the oldest 500 when there are more than 2000). Returns False when it could not be parsed.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By FlightData's /sim/camera/photo_info subscription (ROS thread).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Finds the emulator record a newly saved photo file came from, using the rules of the class (name_time first, then nearest position, then oldest), marks it and every older unmatched record as used, and returns it. When nothing fits it returns None and writes the reason into last_miss (for the log).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.inputs: file_time (the file's modification time), lat/lon from the name, name_time (when the drone was at that GPS, from the MAVROS history).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: For each new photo file, works out the camera pose and zoom at the moment it was taken and the patch of ground it shows (its footprint). Best source first: the camera emulator's own record (exact Gazebo position, orientation, zoom, field of view); otherwise the photo size from the JPEG header, the drone position/height/heading at shutter time from the MAVROS history matched to the file-name GPS, the zoom from zoom.py, and the gimbal straight down (-90 deg) unless configured otherwise.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python. truth_detector, demo_markers and score_run all use this one PhotoGeometry, so the stand-in's boxes, the RViz footprints and the score's 'visible in N photos' always agree. 'flight' is ros_common.FlightData in the nodes and a fake in the tests.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Everything known about one photo's geometry: the photo event, intrinsics (size, field of view, zoom), the camera pose (None if unknown), the MAVROS drone sample used (None if the emulator record was used), how it was found ('emulator', 'gps-match', 'time' or 'none'), where the zoom came from, and the 4 ground corners of the footprint (or None).
The solver that turns a photo event into a PhotoSolution (see the module explanation).

Stores the settings: world origin, the flight-data provider, field of view at zoom 1 (default 1.4137 rad), gimbal pitch (-90) and yaw offset (0), shutter-to-file delay (1 s), the fallback photo size 2560x1440 and the optional emulator photo index.

Works out one photo's geometry and never raises. For a photo that arrived while running, it first finds when the drone was at the file name's GPS (flight.capture_pose); if an emulator record matches, that exact pose and its footprint are returned ('emulator'). Otherwise it reads the JPEG size, looks up the zoom at capture time, builds the pose from the drone sample with truth_model.pose_from_sample (gimbal pitch/yaw offset) and computes the footprint; with no sample the pose and footprint stay None. Photos already in the folder at start are not matched (their time is unknown).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By truth_detector, demo_markers and score_run for every new photo.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: The brain of the truth_detector stand-in. Given one photo's camera pose and the world's answer key, it decides which targets the photo shows, where their boxes are in the picture and how confident a real detector would plausibly be. Rules: at least 50 % of the box inside the photo and at least 12 px long; reported with probability 0.97 (a repeatable pseudo-random draw per photo and target); confidence = class base (person 0.82, tent 0.88) x size factor x edge factor x centre factor + small noise, clipped to 0.30..0.97; a few percent of jitter on the box.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python, unit-tested. It exists because the team's YOLO model was trained on real photos (COCO) and may miss simulated mannequins and tents; the stand-in lets the REST of the mission (main_controller choosing targets, flying there, dropping) be shown anyway. Used by truth_detector; pose_from_sample is also used by photo_geometry for every tool.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The knobs of the stand-in with defaults that look like a decent real detector: min_visible_fraction 0.5, min_pixels 12, good_pixels 60, detect_probability 0.97, base_confidence person 0.82 / tent 0.88, noise_sigma 0.03, min_confidence 0.30 (new_od drops results below 0.25), max_confidence 0.97, box_jitter 0.04 and seed 0 (same seed + same photos = same output).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.how_it_fits: truth_detector fills it from its ROS parameters.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The base confidence of a class from base_confidence (0.82 person, 0.88 tent), or 0.8 for any other class.
One target the stand-in reports in a photo: which truth target it is, its Box (class, score, centre and size in pixels), how much of it is visible (0..1) and how many pixels long it is.

Makes a random-number generator seeded from the photo name, the target name and the seed (through a CRC32 checksum), so the same photo and target always get the same 'random' numbers and a run can be repeated exactly.

The stand-in's confidence formula. Size factor goes from 0.6 at min_pixels (12 px) up to 1.0 at good_pixels (60 px); edge factor is the square root of the visible fraction; centre factor drops by up to 15 % towards the photo corners; confidence = class base x size x edge x centre + noise, clipped to min_confidence..max_confidence (0.30..0.97).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.inputs: cls, pixels (longest side), visible_fraction, center_norm (0 = centre, 1 = corner), noise (already drawn).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Decides which targets one photo shows. For every truth target it builds the 8 corners of its 3D box, projects them into the photo (camera_model.project_box), skips it when less than min_visible_fraction is inside or it is shorter than min_pixels, draws the repeatable 'detected?' dice (detect_probability), then computes the confidence and adds a little jitter to the box centre and size (kept inside the picture).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By truth_detector for every new photo that has a known camera pose.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.outputs: list of TruthHit (empty when no target is visible).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Builds a photo's camera pose from a recorded drone state: position = the sample's GPS converted to Gazebo metres, height = ground + the height above home (40 m if unknown), yaw = the drone heading + the gimbal yaw offset, pitch = the gimbal pitch (-90 = straight down, the emulator keeps it stabilised) and no roll.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By photo_geometry when the camera emulator's exact record is missing.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper): obsolete for the field since 2026-10-31, kept for the legacy option. The ROS 2 node 'truth_detector', the OPTIONAL stand-in for the team's detector (detection/new_od). It watches the same photo folder new_od watches and, for every new photo, publishes the SAME message on the SAME topic: interfaces/ImageResult on /image_detection (RELIABLE, depth 10); only the boxes come from the world's answer key (sim_worlds truth/<world>.yaml) and the camera pose at the shutter moment instead of from the YOLO model. Every message says method = 'truth_detector (stand-in: answer key, not the AI model)'. Like new_od it reports every photo exactly once (also empty ones and ones already in the folder), puts the file-name GPS in latitude/longitude, publishes /sahi_detection_info and answers /sahi/get_statistics and /sahi/get_health.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Started only with detector:=truth (demo_nodes.launch.py / sim.launch.py / demo.sh --detector truth), while sim_bringup points new_od at an always-empty folder so it stays quiet. main_controller cannot tell the difference, so the rest of the mission (hold, divert, drop, RTL) can be shown even when the AI misses simulated targets. With geolocation:=projected it reports the target's own projected position instead, to show what better geolocation would change. The demo panel shows an amber banner while it runs.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper): obsolete for the field since 2026-10-31, kept for the legacy option. The ROS node class: photo folder in, answer-key detections out on /image_detection.

Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Declares the parameters (world runway, worlds_dir, truth_file, photo_dir, poll_period_s 0.5, processing_delay_s 0.5, hfov_rad 1.4137, zoom 0, gimbal_pitch_deg -90, gimbal_yaw_offset_deg 0, capture_latency_s 1.0, geolocation filename, position_noise_m 0.5, the realism knobs, seed 0, include_distractors false), builds the TruthModelConfig, loads the world (a failed load only logs an error; it then reports no targets), finds the photo folder, and sets up the PhotoWatcher, the emulator PhotoInfoIndex, FlightData (MAVROS subscriptions) and PhotoGeometry. Then it creates the /image_detection publisher and a listener on the same topic, the /sahi_detection_info publisher, the two sahi services, a poll timer and a 5 s check for other detectors, and logs 'TRUTH DETECTOR STAND-IN ACTIVE'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Publishers: /image_detection, /sahi_detection_info. Services: /sahi/get_statistics, /sahi/get_health. Subscriptions: /image_detection plus the MAVROS and /sim/camera topics of FlightData.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Logs a warning only the first time a given key is seen, so a repeated problem (no GPS in names, no pose, old photos) does not flood the log.
Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Remembers the last /mavros/mission/reached index; it is copied into each message's waypoint_index like new_od does.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By FlightData when /mavros/mission/reached arrives.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Every 5 s, lists the other nodes that have a publisher on /image_detection and logs once that this is fine while they stay idle (with detector:=truth sim_bringup points new_od at an empty folder).

Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Listens to /image_detection and warns once if ANOTHER detector really publishes results (a method that does not start with 'truth_detector'), because two detectors would make main_controller mix the AI's and the answer key's detections.

Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). The main loop, run every poll_period_s (0.5 s): asks the PhotoWatcher for new photos, queues each one to be processed after processing_delay_s (0.5 s of pretend model time; photos already there at start go without delay), and processes every queued photo whose time has come. An error on one photo is logged and does not stop the node.

Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Handles one photo: takes lat/lon from the file name (0.0 when missing, like new_od), solves the photo geometry, and unless the photo was already there at start or has no known pose, runs truth_model.detect_targets on the answer key (warning when the emulator record did not match and the MAVROS history was used). With geolocation:=projected it replaces lat/lon by the best box centre projected to the ground plus 0.5 m repeatable noise. Then it builds and publishes the ImageResult, updates the counters, publishes a JSON summary on /sahi_detection_info and logs '<photo>: person 0.86 [emulator, zoom 1.0x (camera emulator)]'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Publishes one interfaces/ImageResult on /image_detection and one std_msgs/String on /sahi_detection_info per photo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Answers the /sahi/get_statistics service (std_srvs/Trigger) with a text in new_od's style: 'Images: N, Detections: N, People: N, Tents: N, AvgTime: 0.50s, Errors: 0, Uptime: Ns (truth_detector stand-in)'.

Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Answers the /sahi/get_health service with 'Healthy: True, ConsecErrors: 0, ModelLoaded: True, Format: truth_detector (answer key)' when the world loaded with targets (False otherwise), the same 'ModelLoaded: True' text that sim_bringup's stack_check looks for from new_od.
Legacy (2025) photo pipeline (simulator helper). Entry point of 'ros2 run sim_demo truth_detector': starts rclpy, creates the node, spins it until Ctrl+C or shutdown, then cleans up.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Grades one simulated search mission against the answer key and writes the result as Markdown (score_report.md, for people) and JSON (score_report.json, for scripts). Per target (hiker, tent) it measures: found yes/no, best confidence, in how many photos it was detected and in how many it was visible, the AIM ERROR (main_controller's STATUSTEXT 'Aim <class> <lat>,<lon>' vs the truth; since October 2026 main_controller aims at the ground under the box centre), the old photo GPS error (the detector's reported lat/lon, which is the drone's GPS at the shutter, vs the truth) and the DROP ERROR (where the payload came to rest in Gazebo, or the drone position when the release servo opened, vs the truth). It also counts per-photo true positives, false alarms and misses (precision / recall) and keeps the phase time line.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python. score_run collects the inputs during a flight (or from run_data.json with --rescore) and calls score_run_data, then write_reports. Its JSON keeps 'location_error_m' for older analysis scripts and adds 'aim_error_m'.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: One photo the camera saved during the run: file name, when the file appeared, lat/lon from the name (or None), its ground footprint polygon (or None), how its pose was found ('emulator', 'gps-match', 'time', 'none') and the zoom used.
One payload release: class ('person' or 'tent'), the time the servo opened, the drone's GPS at that moment (or None) and the (east, north) point where the payload came to rest in Gazebo (or None).
Where main_controller said it will drop one payload: class, the time the text arrived and the lat/lon from its STATUSTEXT 'Aim <class> <lat>,<lon>'.

Reads main_controller's status text 'Aim tent 36.2150261,-96.0068008' (sent in _divert_to_targets; 7 decimals = about 1 cm). Returns (class, lat, lon) with class 'person' or 'tent', or None when the text is something else or the numbers are not a position on Earth (|lat| > 90 or |lon| > 180).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By score_run for every /mavros/statustext/send text, and when re-scoring an old run's events.jsonl.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Keeps only the newest aim per class (main_controller sends one per target each time it diverts).

The result for one real target: name, class, true lat/lon, detected?, number of detections, photos_showing (photos whose footprint contained it), best confidence and its photo, seconds until first detected, location_error_m (old photo GPS error), aim_error_m, drop_error_m and where the drop point came from.
Photo-level detection quality for one class: tp (correct detections), fp (false alarms) and fn (misses).
TP / (TP + FP): of all boxes of this class, how many were right. None when nothing was detected.
TP / (TP + FN): of all times a target of this class was in a photo, how often it was found. None when no photo showed this class.

The whole report: world, detector label, start/end times, the TargetScores and ClassScores, what main_controller chose, its aims, the drops, the false detections, photo counts (taken, processed, with detections, footprints known), the time line, notes and the mission map file name.
How long the run lasted in seconds (end minus start, never below 0).
Straight-line distance in metres between two (east, north) points.

Makes a polygon a bit bigger by pushing every corner outwards from its centre by margin metres (score_run_data passes footprint_margin_m, 2 m by default), so a target just outside a photo footprint still counts as shown. An empty polygon or a margin of 0 or less comes back unchanged.

Grades a run against the answer key and returns a RunScore. First it counts how many photo footprints (grown by 2 m) show each target, then judges every detector box: correct (TP) when a real target of its class lies inside that photo's footprint (or, without a footprint, within 50 m of the reported position), otherwise a false alarm (FP), while a target inside a footprint with no box of its class is a miss (FN); per target it keeps the best confidence and that photo's GPS error. Next it measures, per class, the aim error of main_controller's newest 'Aim' text, the photo GPS error of best_per_class (what main_controller chose, with that aim attached), and for every drop the distance from the Gazebo landing point (or the drone position at release) to the nearest target of that class. Last it turns the time line into seconds from the start.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By score_run when it writes the report, and by score_run --rescore.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Formats a number for the report with a unit and a number of decimals; None becomes '-'.
Formats seconds as minutes:seconds, for example 299 -> '4:59'; None becomes '-'.

Writes the report as Markdown: header (world, detector REAL MODEL or TRUTH STAND-IN, run times, targets found, photo counts), the mission map picture link, the Targets table (found, best confidence, detected in / shown in photos, aim error, photo GPS error, drop error), 'What main_controller chose', Payload drops, Detection quality per photo (TP/FP/FN, precision, recall), up to 30 false alarms, the Time line and a section explaining how each number is computed.
The report as a JSON-ready dictionary: every field of RunScore, plus duration_s, precision/recall per class and targets_found.
Creates the run folder if needed and writes score_report.md and score_report.json into it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Writes two files in the run folder.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Finds out where each dropped payload hit the ground in Gazebo, so the report can say 'the tent payload landed 0.3 m from the tent'. PayloadTracker (pure Python) is fed (time, model name, x, y, z) samples and notices when a payload starts falling and when it has come to rest. GzPayloadSubscriber (optional) feeds it from the payloads' own Gazebo odometry topics /sim/payload/person/odometry and /sim/payload/tent/odometry (gz.msgs.Odometry, 10 Hz, world position) using the gz-transport Python bindings directly, without a ROS bridge.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Used by demo_markers (the 'landed' layer) and score_run (drop error). If the gz bindings or topics are missing, score_run falls back to the drone's position when the release servo opened (no wind in the simulation, so the payload falls almost straight down). The odometry comes from the sim_models drone model; payload_release in sim_models does the actual detaching.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Tells which target a payload model is for from its name: the name must contain 'payload', 'drop' or 'bottle', and then 'person', 'hiker' or 'mannequin' means 'person' and 'tent' means 'tent'. Anything else gives None (for example 'payload_tent' -> 'tent').

What is known about one payload model: its Gazebo name, its class, the first position seen, the latest (t, x, y, z), when it started falling (None while still attached) and where it came to rest after falling (None until then).
Watches payload position samples and decides when each payload fell and where it landed. Safe to use from several threads (a lock).

Sets the thresholds: falling = moving down faster than 3 m/s (faster than the drone ever descends in AUTO/RTL; a free fall reaches it after 0.3 s), resting = slower than 0.15 m/s, and it must rest 1.0 s after falling to count as landed.

Feeds one position sample of a model (names that are not payloads are ignored). From the change since the last sample it computes the vertical and total speed: the first time it goes down faster than fall_speed the payload is falling; after that, once it stays slower than rest_speed for rest_time, the current position is stored as the landing point.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By GzPayloadSubscriber's handler for every Gazebo odometry message (10 Hz per payload).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Returns {model name: (t, x, y, z)} for every payload that has landed.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By demo_markers and score_run.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Returns copies of all payload tracks (for reports and markers) so callers never touch the live data.

Feeds a PayloadTracker from the payloads' Gazebo odometry topics using the gz-transport Python bindings (no ROS bridge). GZ_PARTITION / GZ_IP must match the simulator's (sim_env.sh sets astra_sim / 127.0.0.1).
Stores the tracker, the topic list (default /sim/payload/person/odometry and /sim/payload/tent/odometry), a log function and a clock (default time.time); nothing is subscribed yet.
Turns a topic into a model name: '/sim/payload/tent/odometry' -> 'payload_tent' (other shapes: the topic parts joined with '_').

Imports gz.msgs10 Odometry and gz.transport13 Node and subscribes to every topic with a small handler that feeds the tracker. Returns True if at least one subscription worked; if the bindings are missing or anything fails it logs one line ('Gazebo payload tracking off ...') and returns False, never crashing the node.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: At start-up of demo_markers and score_run when gz_payload_tracking is true.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Subscribes to the Gazebo topics /sim/payload/person/odometry and /sim/payload/tent/odometry.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Runs for every Gazebo odometry message of one payload: counts it and passes (now, model name, x, y, z) of the message's position to PayloadTracker.add.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By gz-transport on its own thread, about 10 times per second per payload.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Draws a top-down picture of one mission for the score report (mission_map.png, about 1100 px): the search areas (yellow), every photo's ground footprint (blue), the drone's track (cyan line), where the detector saw targets (dots), what main_controller chose (big rings), where the payloads landed (magenta diamonds) and the REAL targets (red = hiker, orange = tent) with names. North is up, with a 10 m grid, a 10 m scale bar and a north arrow.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Pure Python + Pillow; it takes Gazebo world metres (x east, y north). score_run calls draw_mission_map when it writes the report and links the picture at the top of score_report.md.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Finds the box around all the points to draw, plus a 15 m margin, and makes sure it is at least 60 m wide and tall so the picture is never a thin sliver (default -50..50 m when there are no points).

Draws and saves the map: picks the scale from the bounds, paints the dark background and 10 m grid, then the search areas, footprints, track, detection dots, 'chosen' rings, the REAL target squares with labels, the payload diamonds, the title, a legend, the 10 m scale bar and the north arrow, and saves the PNG.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.inputs: path; targets (name, cls, east, north); areas (name, polygon); footprints; track; detections (cls, east, north, confidence); choices (cls, east, north); drops (cls, east, north, source); title.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Writes mission_map.png.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Converts a world point (east, north in metres) into picture pixels: x grows to the right with east, y grows downwards as north decreases (north is up), with a 20 px left margin and 70 px for the title.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: ROS 2 pieces shared by the sim_demo nodes: the QoS profiles and FlightData, a helper that subscribes to the MAVROS topics describing the drone (state, GPS, height, heading, speed, mission progress, status texts) plus /camera/command, /camera/status and the emulator's /sim/camera/emulator_state and /sim/camera/photo_info, and keeps the latest values in one thread-safe place together with a PoseHistory and a ZoomTracker. QoS: every MAVROS/sensor subscription is BEST_EFFORT (it receives from both reliable and best-effort publishers, so a QoS mismatch can never silently cut a topic); /image_detection uses RELIABLE depth 10 like new_od and main_controller; QOS_LATCHED (RELIABLE + TRANSIENT_LOCAL, depth 1) is for markers a late RViz must still get.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Imported by demo_panel, truth_detector, demo_markers and score_run so they all see the drone the same way. It only listens; it never publishes.
