fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Subscribes to /mavros/state, /mavros/global_position/global, /mavros/global_position/rel_alt, /mavros/global_position/compass_hdg, /mavros/vfr_hud, /mavros/local_position/pose, /mavros/mission/reached, /mavros/mission/waypoints, /mavros/statustext/recv and /send, /camera/command, /camera/status, /sim/camera/emulator_state and (optional) /sim/camera/photo_info, and keeps the newest values. Optional callbacks (on_statustext, on_state, on_reached, on_rel_alt, on_waypoints, on_camera_status) are called on the ROS thread right after the values are stored.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.how_it_fits: Each node passes its own handlers in; photo_geometry uses its capture_pose and zoom.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Creates the lock, a PoseHistory (30 minutes) and a ZoomTracker (fixed zoom if given), sets every value to 'unknown', stores the callbacks and creates all the subscriptions listed for the class (all BEST_EFFORT depth 10; photo_info RELIABLE + TRANSIENT_LOCAL depth 50 so records published before the node started still arrive). subscribe_camera_topics=False leaves out /camera/command and /camera/status.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Creates up to 14 ROS subscriptions on the given node.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Calls one of the optional callbacks by name if it was given; any error in it is logged ('<name> handler failed') instead of stopping the data flow, so a display bug can never break the recording.
Stores connected, armed and mode from /mavros/state with the time, then calls the on_state callback.

Handles a /mavros/global_position/global fix: ignores (0, 0) 'Null Island' and NaN (no GPS lock yet, same rule as video_cam), otherwise stores lat/lon/altitude and adds a PoseSample (with the current height above home, heading and ground speed) to the PoseHistory.
Stores the height above home from /mavros/global_position/rel_alt and calls the on_rel_alt callback.
Stores the compass heading from /mavros/global_position/compass_hdg (0..360 degrees). This source wins over the two fallbacks below.
Stores ground speed and climb rate from /mavros/vfr_hud, and uses its heading only when no compass heading has arrived.

Last-resort heading: when neither compass_hdg nor vfr_hud gave one, turns the /mavros/local_position/pose orientation quaternion into a compass heading (quaternion_to_yaw_deg, then enu_yaw_to_compass_deg).
Stores the last reached mission index (wp_seq) from /mavros/mission/reached and calls the on_reached callback.
Turns /mavros/mission/waypoints (the mission as the autopilot has it) into a list of (command, lat, lon, alt), stores it and calls the on_waypoints callback.

Handles one STATUSTEXT from /mavros/statustext/recv (source 'fcu') or /send (source 'team'): gives it to the ZoomTracker ('Zoom set to 5.0x'), keeps it in the last-500 list and calls the on_statustext callback.
Gives every /camera/command text to the ZoomTracker, which notes 'zoom_absolute N' commands.
Reads the JSON of /sim/camera/emulator_state (camera model, zoom, gimbal angles), feeds zoom.current to the ZoomTracker and stores the whole state with its time.
Passes each /camera/status text (video_cam's replies to commands) to the on_camera_status callback.

Returns a consistent copy of the latest values as a dict (connected, armed, mode, lat, lon, altitude, height above home, heading, ground speed, climb, last reached, and the camera's pitch, yaw, zoom and model from an emulator state not older than 5 s). Safe from any thread.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel's 250 ms GUI timer (telemetry card, HUD) and by demo_markers (drone track and the heading of the drone arrow).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The newest recorded PoseSample (or None), read under the lock. No caller used it at the time of reading.
PoseHistory.capture_pose under the lock, so the ROS thread can keep adding samples while another thread asks where a photo was taken.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By PhotoGeometry.solve for every new photo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Asks the ROS graph which nodes publish on the detector topic /image_detection and returns their names sorted (for example ['new_od'] or ['truth_detector']); [] if the query fails during shutdown.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel (DETECTOR pill, 'TWO detectors!' warning), score_run (report label) and truth_detector (other-detector check).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: The ROS 2 node 'score_run' that records one simulated mission and writes its report card. While the mission runs it listens to /image_detection, MAVROS (through FlightData), the team's status texts (including main_controller's 'Aim <class> <lat>,<lon>'), the photo folder and the payloads' Gazebo odometry; when the drone has landed (plus linger_s = 8 s for late detector messages), on Ctrl+C, or when /sim/demo/write_score is called, it writes into the run folder score_report.md, score_report.json, mission_map.png, run_data.json (all inputs) and keeps events.jsonl (one JSON object per line). 'score_run --rescore DIR' recomputes a finished run offline without ROS.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Started by demo_nodes.launch.py (score:=true); demo.sh passes score:=true and demo_run_dir:=<run folder> (~/.astra_sim/runs/<time>_<world>/) and asks it for the report at the end. The math is in scoring.py, the picture in mission_map.py, payload landing in payloads.py. Default run folder without demo.sh: $ASTRA_RUN_DIR or ~/astra_sim_runs/<world>_<date>_<time>.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Turns an 'Aim <class> <lat>,<lon>' text into an AimRecord and appends it to the list, unless the same class and position were already heard less than 5 s earlier (the same text heard twice, on /mavros/statustext/send and again through the autopilot).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.outputs: The new AimRecord, or None for a non-aim text or a repeat.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Reads a run's events.jsonl line by line and collects every 'Aim' status text it finds (skipping a half-written last line); used to re-score runs recorded before October 2026, whose run_data.json has no 'aims'.
Chooses the run folder when run_dir is empty: $ASTRA_RUN_DIR if set, else ~/astra_sim_runs/<world>_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>.
Rebuilds a DetectionFrame (with its Box list) from the dictionary saved in run_data.json.

Collects everything for the mission map (true targets, search areas, footprints, track, detection points, 'chosen' points and payload drop points) in world metres and calls mission_map.draw_mission_map to write mission_map.png. The 'chosen' rings are main_controller's aim points when known, otherwise the photo position of the best detection (where the old code flew). Any failure only prints a message and returns '' because the report must not depend on the picture.

Recomputes a recorded run's report from its run_data.json without ROS: loads the world (or another world/truth file given on the command line), rebuilds the frames, photos, drops and aims (aims from events.jsonl for older runs), runs score_run_data, redraws the map and rewrites score_report.md/.json.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By 'ros2 run sim_demo score_run --rescore DIR [--world W] [--truth FILE]'.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The ROS part of score_run: imports rclpy and the ROS-side modules only here (so --rescore works without ROS), defines the ScoreRunNode class, spins it, and on shutdown writes the report one last time if it was never written or detections arrived.
The ROS node class 'score_run' that records the run and writes the report.

Declares the parameters (world, worlds_dir, truth_file, photo_dir, run_dir, detector auto, hfov_rad, zoom, gimbal_pitch_deg, finish_on_landed true, linger_s 8.0, gz_payload_tracking true, footprint_margin_m 2.0, geo_match_radius_m 50.0), makes the run folder, loads the world, opens events.jsonl, sets up a PhaseTracker with the mission's lanes, the emulator PhotoInfoIndex, FlightData with its handlers, the PhotoWatcher, PhotoGeometry and the PayloadTracker (+ GzPayloadSubscriber). It then subscribes to /image_detection, offers the /sim/demo/write_score service, starts a 0.5 s tick and a 3 s 'who detects' timer, and logs a 'start' event.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Creates the run folder and events.jsonl; subscribes to /image_detection and the FlightData topics; service /sim/demo/write_score (std_srvs/Trigger).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Appends one line {t, kind, ...data} to events.jsonl and flushes it at once, so the log survives a crash.
For every STATUSTEXT: updates the PhaseTracker, logs a 'statustext' event with the current phase, and if it is main_controller's 'Aim ...' text, records the aim and logs an 'aim' event.

For every /mavros/state: updates the PhaseTracker; on arming remembers the first arming time (the report's start) and logs 'armed'; on disarming logs 'disarmed' and, if the phase is Landed, remembers the landing time (which starts the linger countdown).
Passes /mavros/mission/reached to the PhaseTracker and logs a 'reached' event with the phase.
Passes the height above home to the PhaseTracker.
For every /image_detection message: converts it to a DetectionFrame, keeps it, and logs a 'detection' event with the photo name, lat/lon, method and boxes.
Every 3 s, remembers which nodes publish on /image_detection (new_od or truth_detector) for the report's detector label.

Every 0.5 s: records each new photo (photos already in the folder at start are only counted) with its footprint, pose source and zoom from PhotoGeometry, and logs a 'photo' event. When finish_on_landed is on and linger_s (8 s) have passed since landing, it writes the report once ('the drone landed').
The detector name for the report: the 'detector' parameter if it is 'real' or 'truth'; otherwise 'truth' when any message was from the stand-in or a node named truth_detector published, else 'real'.

Gathers everything the score needs into one dict (saved as run_data.json): start (first arming) and end (landing or now); one DropRecord per drop event, with the drone position looked up just after the last 'Over <class>' text (at most 3 s later, because main_controller's 'Servo' text arrives late) and the Gazebo landing point of that class's payload (landings up to 30 s before the drop event count); the time line (phases, drops, main_controller's chosen plan, armed/disarmed, first detection per class); notes (old photos ignored, no Gazebo poses); the drone track in metres; frames, photos and aims.
Writes the report: saves run_data.json, then (if a world is loaded) runs score_run_data, draws mission_map.png, writes score_report.md and .json, logs the first 16 report lines and a 'report' event.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.outputs: Path of score_report.md ('' without a world).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Writes run_data.json, score_report.md, score_report.json and mission_map.png in the run folder.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Answers the /sim/demo/write_score service: writes the report now and returns success with the report path (or the error text).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: 'ros2 service call /sim/demo/write_score std_srvs/srv/Trigger': by demo.sh's finish() when no score_report.md exists yet (25 s timeout), and by run_reset.py during START OVER to close the old run.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Entry point of 'ros2 run sim_demo score_run'. With --rescore RUN_DIR (and optional --world, --worlds-dir, --truth) it re-scores offline and prints the report; otherwise it starts the ROS node through _ros_main.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: The ROS 2 node 'demo_markers' that draws the search mission in RViz. Twice a second it publishes one visualization_msgs/MarkerArray on /sim/demo/markers (latched, so a late RViz still gets it) with the namespaces search_area (yellow outline), targets (the real hiker red and tent orange, true size, labelled), footprints (blue patches of ground each photo covered, newest outlined), detections (spheres where the detector reported targets), best (what main_controller will fly to), route (the autopilot's mission), track (where the drone flew), drone (an arrow), drops (release points) and landed (payload resting points from Gazebo). Everything is in frame 'world' = Gazebo world ENU with the origin at the SITL home.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Started by demo_nodes.launch.py (markers:=true) next to rviz2 from sim.launch.py. It listens to /image_detection, the FlightData topics, the photo folder (through PhotoGeometry, so footprints match the stand-in and the scorer) and the payloads' Gazebo odometry; it never talks to the team code.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The ROS node class that keeps the mission picture up to date and publishes it to RViz.

Declares the parameters (world, worlds_dir, truth_file, photo_dir, frame_id world, publish_rate_hz 2.0, hfov_rad, zoom, gimbal_pitch_deg -90, max_footprints 800, max_detection_markers 60, track_min_step_m 1.0, gz_payload_tracking true), loads the world and its search areas (or, if the truth file has none, a box around the survey lanes of the mission file), and sets up the PhaseTracker, emulator PhotoInfoIndex, FlightData, a PhotoWatcher (photos already there at start are ignored), PhotoGeometry and the Gazebo payload tracker. Then it subscribes to /image_detection, creates the latched /sim/demo/markers publisher, a 0.5 s photo/track timer and the publish timer.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Publisher /sim/demo/markers (visualization_msgs/MarkerArray, RELIABLE + TRANSIENT_LOCAL); subscriptions /image_detection and the FlightData topics; Gazebo payload odometry.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Converts GPS to world metres (east, north). If no world could be loaded, the first GPS fix becomes the origin so at least the drone track can be drawn.

Feeds every STATUSTEXT to the PhaseTracker; when that produced a new drop event ('Servo 13 -> 1400'), it looks up where the drone was just after the last 'Over <class>' text (at most 3 s later, because main_controller's Servo text arrives late) and stores it as a release point for the 'drops' layer.
Keeps every /image_detection message as a DetectionFrame (dropping the oldest 1000 when there are more than 5000).
Every 0.5 s: solves the footprint of each new photo (keeping the newest 800) and adds the drone's current position to the track whenever it moved at least 1 m.
Makes one empty RViz Marker with the given namespace, id, type and colour in the fixed frame, stamped now, scale 1.
Makes a geometry_msgs/Point from x, y, z.
Makes a text marker that always faces the camera (TEXT_VIEW_FACING) at a position, with a size.

Builds and publishes the whole MarkerArray (the first time preceded by DELETEALL to clear old markers): search area outlines and names, true targets as boxes with an 8 m ring and a 'HIKER (name)' / 'TENT (name)' label, all photo footprints faint plus the newest outlined, the newest 60 detection spheres, a big 'BEST PERSON 0.92 (flies here)' sphere per class at the photo GPS of best_per_class, the mission route (from MAVROS, else the file; NAV items only), the track line and the drone arrow pointing along its heading, release cylinders and Gazebo landing spheres.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: Every 1 / publish_rate_hz seconds (0.5 s by default).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Publishes /sim/demo/markers.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Entry point of 'ros2 run sim_demo demo_markers': starts rclpy, creates the node and spins it until Ctrl+C or shutdown.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: What the panel's UPLOAD MISSION + START and RTL buttons do, on a background thread so the window never freezes. Start sequence (the job a pilot does in Mission Planner): 1) connect to the autopilot with pymavlink on udpin:127.0.0.1:14553 (an extra MAVProxy output), 2) upload the world's .waypoints mission with the MAVLink mission protocol (MISSION_ITEM_INT), 3) ask MAVROS to re-read it (/mavros/mission/pull) so waypoint_manager and main_controller learn the new indices, 4) switch to GUIDED and retry arming through the SITL settling time ('Arm: Gyros inconsistent' for ~30 s is normal), 5) MAV_CMD_MISSION_START (300) so ArduCopter goes AUTO and takes off. Without a MAVLink answer the same steps run through MAVROS services (/mavros/mission/push, /mavros/set_mode, /mavros/cmd/arming, /mavros/cmd/command). RTL = set mode RTL.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: ROS-free (the MAVROS path goes through an adapter object the panel passes in: demo_panel.MavrosAdapter). It replaces the pilot only in the simulator: the team code never arms or takes off by itself. MAVLink goes to MAVProxy, which forwards it to ArduPilot SITL.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: A background worker for mission upload + start and RTL. Its request methods return at once and can be called from the Qt thread; progress is reported through a status(text, level) callback with level 'info', 'ok', 'warn' or 'error'. 'link' picks the path: 'auto' (MAVLink, else MAVROS), 'mavlink' or 'mavros'.

Stores the MAVLink URL, the status callback, the optional MAVROS adapter and the link choice, uses MAVLink system id 252 / component 191 (not a ground station's usual 255, probably so it is not mixed up with Mission Planner), sets 3 s between arming attempts and an 8 s heartbeat wait in 'auto' mode, and prepares a job queue, a re-entrant lock (one MAVLink exchange at a time) and the worker thread.
Starts the worker thread.
Stops the worker thread (waiting requests are dropped) and closes the MAVLink connection.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: When the panel closes.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Queues the start sequence with the mission items, the settle timeout (default 150 s) and an optional before_arm step (the panel uses it to send LOOK DOWN). Returns False when a start sequence is already running.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: When UPLOAD MISSION + START is pressed (or by auto_start).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Sends RTL on its own short thread, so it works even while a start sequence is still waiting to arm.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: When RTL (FLY HOME) is pressed.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The worker loop: takes jobs from the queue and runs the start sequence; any error is reported as 'Start sequence failed: ...' instead of killing the thread, and busy is cleared afterwards.

Decides whether to talk MAVLink: never in 'mavros' mode or without a URL; otherwise connects once (8 s heartbeat wait in 'auto', 30 s in 'mavlink') and reports 'No MAVLink heartbeat on that port - using MAVROS services instead.' when nothing answers.
Opens the pymavlink connection (auto-reconnect) and waits for a HEARTBEAT; returns the connection or None (also when pymavlink is not installed, which is reported).

The start steps: check there is a mission and a reachable link; upload (MAVLink or MAVROS push); ask MAVROS to pull the mission; run before_arm (LOOK DOWN); set GUIDED; retry arming until settle_timeout_s; send MAV_CMD_MISSION_START (or, if refused, switch to AUTO). Each step reports a status line such as 'Mission uploaded.' or 'ARMED. Starting the mission (AUTO) ...'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: MAVLink to the autopilot (mission upload, DO_SET_MODE, ARM, MISSION_START) or the MAVROS services; /mavros/mission/pull.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Runs the MAVLink mission upload while holding the MAVLink lock.

The MAVLink mission upload dance: sends MISSION_COUNT, then answers every MISSION_REQUEST(_INT) from the autopilot with that item as MISSION_ITEM_INT (lat/lon times 1e7), until MISSION_ACK. Accepted (type 0) means success; any other ACK is reported as a rejection; a lost first request is retried; it gives up after 30 s.
Sends one MAVLink COMMAND_LONG and waits up to 3 s for its COMMAND_ACK; True only when the result is ACCEPTED (0). STATUSTEXTs that arrive meanwhile are checked for an arming refusal reason.
Remembers an autopilot text that starts with 'PreArm', 'Arm' or 'Prearm' as the last reason why arming failed (shown as 'Not ready to arm yet (Arm: Gyros inconsistent)').
Changes the flight mode: through MAVROS set_mode, or with MAVLink MAV_CMD_DO_SET_MODE (176) using ArduCopter's mode numbers (GUIDED 4, AUTO 3, RTL 6, LAND 9 ...).

Tries to arm (MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM 400, or MAVROS arming) every 3 s until it works or the timeout ends, reporting 'Not ready to arm yet (...); retrying (N s left)' on the 1st, 4th, 7th ... try.
Sends RTL mode through whichever link works (existing MAVLink connection, else MAVROS, else a new MAVLink connection) and reports 'RTL commanded: flying home.' or 'RTL command FAILED.'.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: Opens, closes and checks Mission Planner (the Windows ground-station program the team flies with) from Ubuntu inside WSL, using WSL 'interop', which lets a Linux program start Windows .exe files. It only ever runs three Windows programs: tasklist.exe (is MissionPlanner.exe running? it only looks), taskkill.exe (please close; with /F close now) and MissionPlanner.exe itself. Before opening it copies the ASTRA plugin (simulation/windows/mission_planner_plugin/astra_gcs.cs) into Mission Planner's plugins folder. Every check returns a Result with a short sentence; normal problems (not in WSL, not installed, interop off, Windows slow) never raise.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: No ROS, no Qt. Used by the demo panel's OPEN / CLOSE MISSION PLANNER buttons and its 'Mission Planner: running' light (through MissionPlannerMonitor, a 2 s background checker), and by simulation/scripts/mission_planner.sh (python3 -m sim_demo.mission_planner start|stop|status). Closing Mission Planner never disturbs the simulated drone: its autopilot has FS_GCS_ENABLE 0 (no ground-station failsafe) in sim_models/config/astra_sitl.parm.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Wraps a Windows command so a tiny /bin/sh, not Python, changes into the C: folder and starts it. Reason: Python holds its global lock while starting a child process, and the slow cd into /mnt/c plus the interop exec froze the panel's live camera every few seconds; letting /bin/sh do it keeps the video smooth.
subprocess.run for Windows programs, routed through _via_shell so the panel does not freeze.
subprocess.Popen for Windows programs, routed through _via_shell so the panel does not freeze.

What a check or action found out (frozen): ok (the question was answered / the action worked), message (one sentence for people), running (is Mission Planner open: True, False or None = could not tell) and label (two or three words for the status light, e.g. 'not running').
True when this Linux runs inside WSL on Windows: /proc/version then contains 'microsoft' (for example '5.15.167.4-microsoft-standard-WSL2').

Turns a Windows path into the path Ubuntu sees, for example 'C:\Tools\MissionPlanner.exe' -> '/mnt/c/Tools/MissionPlanner.exe'; Linux paths come back unchanged. So MISSION_PLANNER_EXE can be pasted straight from the Windows file explorer.

The places find_exe looks for MissionPlanner.exe: a given path (panel parameter mission_planner_exe or --exe), else $MISSION_PLANNER_EXE, REPLACES the usual install folders (so a typo is reported, not silently ignored); otherwise '/mnt/c/Program Files (x86)/Mission Planner/MissionPlanner.exe' and '/mnt/c/Program Files/Mission Planner/MissionPlanner.exe'.
Returns the first existing MissionPlanner.exe among exe_candidates, or None.
Finds a Windows command such as tasklist.exe on the PATH, or directly in /mnt/c/Windows/System32 when WSL does not add Windows folders to the PATH; None if missing.
Builds the sentence shown when MissionPlanner.exe is missing, naming every searched place and how to fix it (install from ardupilot.org or set MISSION_PLANNER_EXE / mission_planner_exe).

Answers 'can OPEN / CLOSE work on this computer?' by looking only at files (quick, starts nothing): not in WSL -> label 'not on Windows'; no exe -> 'not installed'; else 'installed'. The reason becomes the tooltip of the greyed-out buttons.
The first non-empty line of a program's output, cut to 160 characters, for short error sentences.

Runs tasklist.exe or taskkill.exe through WSL interop with a 10 s timeout, from the program's own C: folder (a Windows program started from a Linux folder would get a network path). Returns (finished process, '') or (None, a sentence: Windows did not answer in time, or interop seems off).

Pulls the process ids of MissionPlanner.exe out of tasklist.exe's output, in the CSV form that is asked for ('"MissionPlanner.exe","46792",...') or the plain table form. Windows' 'No tasks are running ...' sentence matches no row, so the Windows language does not matter.

Asks Windows whether Mission Planner is open: runs 'tasklist.exe /FI "IMAGENAME eq MissionPlanner.exe" /FO CSV /NH' (about 0.3 s) and returns Result running True ('Mission Planner is running (Windows process N).') or False, or ok=False with the reason (not WSL, tasklist missing, Windows did not answer).

Searches upward from this file for simulation/windows/mission_planner_plugin/astra_gcs.cs (the ASTRA Mission Planner plugin, which adds the ASTRA tab and the camera in the HUD) and returns its path, or None.

Copies astra_gcs.cs into the 'plugins' folder next to MissionPlanner.exe when it is missing or different (Mission Planner compiles every .cs file there when it starts, so this must happen BEFORE it opens). Returns a sentence ('ASTRA plugin installed: the ASTRA tab is on the DATA screen.', 'up to date', 'updated', or how to fix a failed copy with simulation/windows/install_mp_plugin.ps1) and never raises.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: May write <Mission Planner folder>/plugins/astra_gcs.cs on the Windows disk.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Starts a daemon thread that waits for WSL's small helper process of the started Windows program, so it never lingers as a 'zombie' after Mission Planner closes.

Opens Mission Planner unless it is already open (one copy is enough). It checks availability, installs the plugin, then starts MissionPlanner.exe DETACHED: its own session (Ctrl+C does not reach it), no terminal or pipe, no ASTRA_SIM_SESSION tag (so stop_sim.sh never closes it) and its own folder as working directory. It then watches the task list for up to 8 s and returns 'Mission Planner is opening (its window takes 10-30 s). In Mission Planner: UDP -> CONNECT -> port 14550. ...'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Starts the Windows program MissionPlanner.exe; may copy the ASTRA plugin.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Checks the task list every 0.5 s until Mission Planner is gone (True) or the time is up (False); a check Windows does not answer counts as 'not gone yet'.

Closes Mission Planner: first politely with 'taskkill.exe /IM MissionPlanner.exe' (like clicking its X, so it can save its settings), and only if it is still open 5 s later, forced with 'taskkill.exe /F /IM MissionPlanner.exe'. Returns 'Mission Planner closed.', 'was forced to close (...)' or why it could not.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Closes the Windows program MissionPlanner.exe.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The latest picture for the panel (frozen, so the Qt thread can read it safely): checked, available (buttons can work), running (True/False/None), busy ('', 'opening' or 'closing'), label for the status light and the full message for the tooltip.

A background thread for the demo panel: every 2 s it checks whether Mission Planner runs, and it carries out OPEN / CLOSE presses one at a time, so the window never waits for Windows (starting a program takes seconds). The Qt thread only calls request_open(), request_close() and snapshot().

Stores the report(text, level) callback (called from the worker thread, so it must not touch Qt widgets), the exe override and the check period (2 s), and prepares the lock, the starting PlannerState ('checking ...'), the job queue and the worker thread.
Starts the worker thread; the first check begins at once.
Stops the worker thread; an action already running finishes by itself.
Returns the latest PlannerState (immutable, safe from any thread).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel's 250 ms GUI timer to colour the light and grey out buttons.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Queues OPEN; returns False (and does nothing) while another action is still running.
Queues CLOSE; returns False (and does nothing) while another action is still running.
Marks the state busy ('opening' / 'closing') and queues the job, unless something is already busy.
The worker loop: check, then wait up to period_s (2 s) for a button press; a press is carried out at once, otherwise the next check runs.
One check: availability() and, if that is fine, is_running(); stores the result as the new PlannerState (an unexpected error becomes the message instead of killing the thread).

Carries out one press with start() or stop() (up to about 10 s of waiting for Windows), takes over the found running state at once so the buttons do not flicker, clears busy and reports the result sentence.

Command line 'python3 -m sim_demo.mission_planner start|stop|status [--exe PATH]': prints one sentence; exit code 0 = done (status: running), 1 = failed or cannot tell, 3 = status: not running (like systemctl status).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By simulation/scripts/mission_planner.sh.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: The building blocks of the demo window, drawn with PyQt5: VideoView (the big live camera picture with a heads-up display, a crosshair and a white PHOTO flash), PhotoView (the newest photo with the detector's boxes and labels), PhaseStrip (Waiting > Taking off > ... > Landed with the current phase lit), StatusPill (small coloured status labels), EventLog (the scrolling colour-coded event list), the dark colour theme (THEME, STYLE_SHEET) and ros_image_to_qimage, which turns the raw bytes of a sensor_msgs/Image into a Qt image WITHOUT OpenCV (the pip OpenCV build changes Qt's plugin path and breaks PyQt5).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Nothing here talks to ROS; demo_panel.py builds the window from these widgets and feeds them from its 250 ms GUI timer.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Turns the raw fields of a sensor_msgs/Image (encoding, width, height, row step, bytes) into a QImage that owns a copy of its pixels. Supports rgb8, bgr8 (colours swapped), rgba8, bgra8, mono8, 8UC1 and 8UC3; returns None for other encodings or sizes that do not add up.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the panel for each /sim/camera/image frame it shows (the live view is 1280x720 at 25 Hz).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Wraps a widget in a rounded dark card with a small upper-case title (and an optional widget at the right of the title, such as the Mission Planner light).
Makes a DejaVu Sans font of a given pixel size, optionally bold.
Draws a piece of text on a small rounded coloured background at a point (used for the LIVE CAMERA POV badge, box labels like 'PERSON 86%', 'TARGET FOUND' ...) and returns the rectangle it used.
The largest rectangle with the picture's width-to-height ratio that fits centred inside an area, so pictures are never stretched.
The live camera picture widget (keeps its aspect ratio) with a heads-up display.
Sets the minimum size 480x270 and the starting state: no picture, placeholder 'Waiting for the camera picture ...'.
Changes the text shown while there is no picture.
Shows a new camera frame and remembers the frame rate and when it arrived (to say NO SIGNAL after 3 s without frames).
Stores the heads-up values: height (m), speed, heading, flight mode, armed, camera pitch and zoom (any may be missing).
Starts the white border flash with a label such as 'PHOTO #12', meaning a photo was just taken.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: When a new photo lands in the team photo folder.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Draws the widget: black background, the picture fitted to the widget (or the placeholder text), a crosshair, a red 'LIVE CAMERA POV' badge (grey 'NO SIGNAL' when no frame came for 3 s), the resolution and fps, the HUD bar 'ALT 30.1 m (99 ft) | SPD 5.5 m/s | HDG 090 | AUTO | ARMED | CAM -90 1.0x' and, for 0.9 s after a photo, the fading white flash.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By Qt whenever the widget must be repainted.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The photo widget: a photo with detection boxes, plus a caption bar.
Sets the minimum size 320x180 and the starting placeholder 'No photos yet. Photos appear here when the drone takes them.'.
Changes the text shown while there is no photo (the panel puts the photo folder path in it).

Shows a photo (possibly shrunk) with its full-resolution size (the boxes are in full-resolution pixels), a caption, the Box list, a right-hand status text and colour, an optional green 'target found' frame and extra text lines (listed on the photo when the detector named other things but no person/tent).

Draws the photo fitted to the widget, each box scaled from full-resolution pixels in its class colour (red person, orange tent) with a label like 'TENT 88%' (tiny boxes also get a dashed 22 px ring so they stay visible), the extra lines, the green TARGET FOUND frame, and the caption bar with the status on the right and the file name shortened in the middle when it does not fit.
The row of mission phases: the current one is lit blue, passed ones are ticked green, skipped ones say '(skipped)', and a line below explains the phase.
Stores the phase names (the 8 PHASES from phases.py) and starts at phase 0 (Waiting).
Updates which phase is lit, which phases were visited, the detail sentence and the '(for 1:21)' text, then repaints.

Draws one rounded chip per phase with arrows between them (font shrinks until the name fits), colouring current / done / skipped / future chips, and the cyan line 'Searching: lane 2 of 3   (for 1:21)' underneath.
A small rounded label with a name and a coloured state: ok = green, warn = amber, bad = red, off = grey (used for MAVROS, CAMERA, PHOTOS, DETECTOR).
Stores the pill's name and starts it grey with 'waiting'.
Sets the text to '● NAME: text', the colour from the state and an optional tooltip.

A read-only, colour-coded event list (newest at the bottom, scrolls by itself, keeps the last 400 lines): autopilot cyan, team white, camera yellow, panel green, detector orange, start over violet, warnings amber, errors red.
Makes the text box read-only, limited to 400 lines, with line wrapping.
Appends one line 'HH:MM:SS [source] text' coloured by level or source (text safely escaped) and scrolls to the bottom.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: The ROS 2 node 'demo_panel' and its PyQt5 window 'ASTRA Simulation - Search Demo', the screen people watch. It shows the big live camera (/sim/camera/image) with height, speed, heading and mode, the newest photo from the team folder with the detector's boxes (matched to /image_detection by file name), the detection list and 'what main_controller will fly to', the mission phase strip, telemetry, an event log and the status pills MAVROS / CAMERA / PHOTOS / DETECTOR (with an amber banner while the truth stand-in is the detector). Its buttons: TAKE PHOTO (/camera/trigger), LOOK DOWN / LOOK FORWARD (/camera/command 'gimbal_set_angles 0,-90' / '0,0'), UPLOAD MISSION + START and RTL (mission_control.py), START OVER (two clicks within 5 s, runs simulation/scripts/start_over.sh -> run_reset.py) and OPEN / CLOSE MISSION PLANNER (mission_planner.py). Nothing blocks the window: ROS spins on a background thread, autopilot commands, Mission Planner checks and photo loading each have their own worker.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: The OLD ground screen: since 2026-10-24 (commit 83c2ae4) demo.sh leaves it off unless --panel, because Mission Planner with the ASTRA plugin is the ground station now; sim.launch.py's own panel argument still defaults to true (for example start_sim.sh by hand). When it runs it is started by demo_nodes.launch.py (panel:=true) inside sim.launch.py. Its photo, detection and TAKE PHOTO parts follow the legacy (2025) photo pipeline (video_cam photos, /image_detection from new_od). It mostly LISTENS (FlightData MAVROS topics, /image_detection, /camera/trigger, the photo folder) and acts through the same doors the ground crew uses: /camera/trigger and /camera/command (video_cam does the work), MAVLink to MAVProxy's extra output udp:127.0.0.1:14553 (fallback: MAVROS services), and Windows programs through WSL interop. Screenshots can be taken offscreen (screenshot_path); test/ros_e2e/run_fake_mission_e2e.sh and test/render_panel_preview.py use that.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Makes PyQt5 start reliably before the QApplication exists: removes QT_QPA_PLATFORM_PLUGIN_PATH / QT_QPA_FONTDIR if they point into a cv2 folder (the pip OpenCV build sets them and the system PyQt5 then crashes with 'could not load the Qt platform plugin xcb'), and with no screen at all (no DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY) draws offscreen so screenshots still work. Returns a note for the log.

Decides what the DETECTOR pill and the stand-in banner show, from the messages actually received (their method): both kinds -> red 'TWO detectors!'; only stand-in -> amber 'STAND-IN'; only real -> green 'REAL (new_od)'. Before any message it goes by which nodes publish /image_detection; with nobody -> grey 'not running'. A publisher that never publishes does not count, because detector:=truth keeps new_od running but idle on an empty folder.

The MAVROS service calls used as the fallback path of the mission buttons: /mavros/set_mode, /mavros/cmd/arming, /mavros/cmd/command, /mavros/mission/push and /mavros/mission/pull. Safe to call from any thread except the ROS executor thread (it waits for answers).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.how_it_fits: Handed to mission_control.MissionCommander, which uses it when no MAVLink heartbeat answers on 14553 and to ask MAVROS to re-read the mission after an upload.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Creates the five MAVROS service clients (SetMode, CommandBool, CommandLong, WaypointPush, WaypointPull) on the panel node.
True when MAVROS answers, judged by whether its /mavros/set_mode service is ready.

Calls a service and waits (up to the timeout, default 10 s) for the answer by polling every 0.05 s on the caller's thread; returns None when the service is missing (2 s wait) or does not answer in time.
Uploads the mission items through /mavros/mission/push (start_index 0), turning each MissionItem into a mavros_msgs/Waypoint (item 0 marked current). True when MAVROS reports success.
Asks MAVROS to re-read the mission from the autopilot (/mavros/mission/pull), so the team's waypoint_manager and main_controller see the new mission (MAVROS never re-reads after an upload by itself).
Changes the flight mode with /mavros/set_mode using ArduPilot's mode names (GUIDED, AUTO, RTL ...); True when the mode was sent.
Tries to arm with /mavros/cmd/arming (value true) and returns (accepted, reason), e.g. 'arming refused (result 4)' or 'MAVROS arming service did not answer'.
Sends a MAVLink COMMAND_LONG (command number + 7 parameters) through /mavros/cmd/command, for example MAV_CMD_MISSION_START; True on success.

The panel's side of START OVER (the work itself is run_reset.py): launch() starts simulation/scripts/start_over.sh --no-fresh in the background, detached (its own session, so it keeps running if the panel closes; stop_sim.sh still finds it by the session tag), and poll() reads the progress lines it writes through run_reset.ProgressTracker. The Qt thread only reads a small file, so the window never waits.

Imports run_reset, picks the launcher (run_reset.launch_start_over, or a fake in tests), opens a ProgressTracker on the progress file in the simulator's state folder and skips the history already in it (so an active reset's lockout is restored without replaying old lines).
True while a START OVER runs, also one started from a terminal with start_over.sh.
Step counter text like '5/14' while a reset runs ('' before its first step).
Starts start_over.sh --no-fresh in the background and returns its log file path (raises OSError if bash is missing).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Starts the bash script simulation/scripts/start_over.sh as a detached process.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Returns the new progress updates (run_reset.ProgressUpdate list, oldest first).

After launch(): '' while the script still runs; if it already ended without writing progress, the last line of its log with terminal colour codes removed (for example 'sim_demo is not built'), or 'no output'.
The ROS side of the panel (no Qt here): parameters, subscriptions, publishers and the mission state (PhaseTracker, detection frames, latest camera image, shutter count, event queue).

Declares the panel parameters (world, worlds_dir, truth_file, photo_dir, camera_topic /sim/camera/image, detector, mavlink_url udpin:127.0.0.1:14553, mission_link auto, auto_start false, auto_start_delay_s 5, settle_timeout_s 150, look_down_on_start true, the two gimbal commands, hit_hold_s 8, window 1600 x 960, fullscreen, screenshot settings, mission_planner_exe), loads the world and its mission (giving the PhaseTracker the lanes), finds the photo folder, creates FlightData with its handlers, subscribes to the camera image, /image_detection and /camera/trigger, creates the /camera/trigger and /camera/command publishers and the MavrosAdapter, and starts a 2 s detector check.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Subscribes to /sim/camera/image (BEST_EFFORT depth 2), /image_detection (RELIABLE 10), /camera/trigger and the FlightData topics; publishes /camera/trigger (std_msgs/Bool) and /camera/command (std_msgs/String); MAVROS service clients.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Adds a line (time, source, text, level) to the event queue that the window's timer moves into the Events list (thread-safe; keeps the last 600).

Forgets the old run when START OVER begins or ends: a new PhaseTracker (with the same mission lanes), no detections, no last hit, shutter count 0. The subscriptions stay, because the new autopilot and team stack come back on the same topics.
Every 2 s, stores which nodes publish /image_detection (for the DETECTOR pill and the 'detector: checking this photo ...' caption).
Keeps only the newest /sim/camera/image message, counts frames and records arrival times (for the fps and the CAMERA pill); the Qt thread converts it later.
Counts every 'true' on /camera/trigger, whether from the panel's TAKE PHOTO or from the team's mission_camera_trigger (1 Hz during the search), shown as 'Photos saved (shutter presses)'.

For every /image_detection message: converts it to a DetectionFrame, stores it by photo name and in a queue for the table, remembers the last frame with boxes (the 'last hit') and logs 'TENT 88% in <photo>' (+ '(stand-in)') in Events.

Feeds every STATUSTEXT to the PhaseTracker and logs it as 'autopilot' (/recv) or 'team' (/send), amber for PreArm/Arm:/failed/warn texts; very frequent team texts ('No objects detected', 'SUCCESS: Captured', 'Simulation photo captured') are not listed.
Feeds /mavros/state to the PhaseTracker and logs changes: 'MAVROS connected to the autopilot' / 'lost', 'ARMED - motors on' / 'DISARMED - motors off', 'Flight mode: AUTO'.
Feeds /mavros/mission/reached to the PhaseTracker.
Feeds the height above home to the PhaseTracker.

When the autopilot's mission arrives on /mavros/mission/waypoints and the flight is still in Waiting, Taking off or Searching, re-analyses it (mission_file.analyze with the config's hold point) so the lane numbers follow the mission really loaded.
Logs each /camera/status reply from video_cam in Events as 'camera' (amber when it contains FAIL or ERROR).
TAKE PHOTO: publishes true on the team's /camera/trigger topic, so video_cam asks the camera (the emulator) for a photo and downloads it exactly like in flight.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Publishes std_msgs/Bool(true) on /camera/trigger.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Publishes a text on the team's /camera/command topic (for example 'gimbal_set_angles 0,-90' for LOOK DOWN) and logs it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Publishes std_msgs/String on /camera/command.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The Qt window, built only when the panel runs (so importing the module needs no display). Tests can pass fake Mission Planner and START OVER helpers so they never touch Windows or run scripts.

Builds the whole window (minimum 1200 x 760): header with title, world and hidden targets, the four status pills, the amber stand-in banner, the phase strip, the live camera card, the photo card with Auto / Newest / Last hit buttons, the Detections card (best line + table), and the bottom row Telemetry | Controls (TAKE PHOTO, LOOK DOWN, LOOK FORWARD, UPLOAD MISSION + START, RTL (FLY HOME), START OVER, OPEN/CLOSE MISSION PLANNER, connect hint, status line, Mission Planner light) | Events. Then it starts the MissionCommander, the MissionPlannerMonitor and the StartOverLink, and the Qt timers: video 40 ms, UI 250 ms, photos 500 ms, START OVER progress 500 ms (plus auto-start and screenshot timers if asked).
Switches the photo card to Auto, Newest or Last hit and forces a redraw.
Clicking a detection row pins that row's photo in the photo card (mode 'pinned') and un-ticks the mode buttons.
TAKE PHOTO button: publishes the trigger through the node and flashes 'PHOTO REQUESTED' on the live view.

Receives status sentences from the mission worker and the Mission Planner worker: stores the text for the status line (shown by the 250 ms timer, since it may run on another thread) and logs it in Events.

UPLOAD MISSION + START: refuses while START OVER runs or a start sequence is already running; otherwise asks the MissionCommander to upload the world's mission and start it with the settle timeout (150 s by default). With look_down_on_start (the default) it also hands over a 'before' step that sends LOOK DOWN after the upload and before arming.
The step run just before arming: sends the LOOK DOWN gimbal command ('gimbal_set_angles 0,-90') so the photos point at the ground.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By MissionCommander._start_sequence on its worker thread, after the upload and before GUIDED/arming.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: RTL (FLY HOME) button: asks the MissionCommander for RTL and logs 'RTL requested'.
True from the confirming START OVER click until the reset has finished (also a reset started in a terminal).

START OVER button: the first click arms it for 5 s and explains what will happen; the second click within 5 s launches start_over.sh in the background (returns at once). It refuses while a reset or the start sequence is running.

Every 0.5 s reads START OVER's new progress lines: at the start of a reset and when it finishes it clears the old run from the screen, puts step lines into Events (detail lines only into the status line), shows 'START OVER 5/14: ...', 'START OVER done: ... New run: <folder>' or 'START OVER FAILED: ...', and reports 'START OVER did not start' if the script ended without progress or gave no reply within 60 s.

Forgets the old run on screen: node state (phases, detections), the table, the best line, the photo list, the photo cache and pending loads (the photo generation number goes up so late loads are ignored), and shows an empty photo card. The windows stay open.

Sets START OVER's text, colour, tooltip and clickability ('STARTING OVER 5/14 ...', amber 'CLICK AGAIN TO START OVER (3 s)', or 'START OVER'), cancels an unconfirmed first click after 5 s, and locks UPLOAD MISSION + START while a reset runs. It only restyles when something changed.
OPEN MISSION PLANNER: hands the press to the Mission Planner worker thread (returns at once) and says 'Opening Mission Planner on Windows ...'.
CLOSE MISSION PLANNER: hands the press to the worker thread and says 'Closing Mission Planner on Windows ...'.

Saves the window as a PNG at screenshot_path (numbered _01, _02 ... when screenshot_count > 1), repeats every screenshot_every_s until enough pictures exist, and then quits the app if quit_after_screenshot is set. Works offscreen.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Writes PNG files.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Every 40 ms: if a new camera frame arrived, converts it with ros_image_to_qimage, computes the frame rate from the last 60 arrival times and shows it (or says the encoding is unsupported).
Every 0.5 s: for each new photo in the team folder, adds it to the photo list and flashes 'PHOTO #n' on the live view (photos already there at start are not counted).

Runs on the photo-loader thread: reads a photo with QImageReader, letting the JPEG decoder shrink it to at most 1600 px while decoding, and returns it with its full size and the photo generation it was asked for.
On the Qt thread: takes finished photo loads from the worker, drops ones from before a START OVER, and keeps the newest 12 in a cache.

Decides which photo to show: Pinned = the clicked row's photo; Last hit = the last photo with a target; Newest = always the newest; Auto = while Processing photos, Flying to target or Dropping, the photo of the detection main_controller flies to ('flying to this tent'), else a fresh hit for hit_hold_s (8 s), else the newest photo.

Shows the chosen photo with its boxes from the matching /image_detection frame: starts a background load if it is not cached yet; captions it '[AUTO] photo 12/40 <name>' with a status such as '1 target found', 'no targets in this photo', 'detector: checking this photo ...' or 'no detector running' (+ '(stand-in)'); lists the detector's other classes when there are no person/tent boxes. Redraws only when something changed.

Every 250 ms: updates the phase strip (with 'for m:ss'), telemetry (link, mode, motors, height in m and ft, speed, heading, GPS, 'photos (shutter presses)'), the HUD, the four pills and the stand-in banner, the Mission Planner light, new rows in the detection table (newest on top, max 300), the 'N DETECTIONS IN M CHECKED PHOTOS' counter, the 'main_controller will fly to' line, the photo card, up to 200 queued event lines, the START OVER button and the status line.

Colours the Mission Planner light and enables the buttons from the worker's latest snapshot only (no Windows call on the Qt thread): OPEN only while it is closed, CLOSE only while it is open, neither while busy or when this computer cannot do it; tooltips explain why.
Stops the timers, the mission worker, the Mission Planner worker and the photo loader when the app quits. Mission Planner itself stays open.

Entry point of 'ros2 run sim_demo demo_panel': prepares the Qt environment, starts rclpy without its own signal handlers, creates the PanelNode, spins it on a 3-thread executor in a background thread, creates the QApplication and the DemoWindow (fullscreen if asked), makes Ctrl+C / SIGTERM quit the app, runs the Qt loop and cleans up.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: The ROS 2 node 'pov_server' that shows the drone's camera inside Mission Planner. Mission Planner cannot read a ROS topic but can show an MJPEG web stream, so this node re-encodes the newest /sim/camera/image picture as a JPEG (at most 10 per second, shrunk to 960 px wide, quality 75) and serves it over plain HTTP on this computer only: http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg (the live stream), /pov.jpg (one picture), / (a help page) and /health (a status line). By default it draws a small box with the gimbal angles on every picture: line 1 = pitch/yaw/roll the way the SIYI camera reports them (from the measured joints /sim/gimbal/joint_states and the drone attitude /sim/drone/odometry), line 2 = the raw joint angles relative to the drone.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Started by sim_bringup's sim.launch.py (pov_server:=true by default, pov_port:=8082 moves it), not by demo_nodes.launch.py. It only READS topics; a crash here changes nothing else. The ASTRA Mission Planner plugin (simulation/windows/mission_planner_plugin/astra_gcs.cs) shows this stream in the HUD by itself (its astra_camera_url defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg and it checks /health first); without the plugin: right-click the HUD > Video > Set MJPEG Source > that address (WSL forwards localhost). It shows the twin's simulated live camera, not the field camera's RTSP stream (the new video pipeline's simulator side is being built separately). Its angle formulas match siyi_emulator's GimbalModel.reported_attitude (a test compares them). Everything except main() is tested without ROS (test/test_pov_server.py).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Turns a ROS image (width, height, encoding rgb8/bgr8/rgba8/bgra8/mono8, row length, bytes) into JPEG bytes: handles padded rows, swaps BGR to RGB, drops the alpha channel, shrinks to max_width (960 px) when wider, optionally draws the overlay text box, and saves with the given quality (kept within 10..95). Raises ValueError for an unsupported encoding or too little data, so a corrupt message is skipped instead of producing garbage.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By main's on_image callback for each camera picture that passes the max_fps limit.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Returns a readable bold font of about the given pixel size: DejaVu Sans Bold (Ubuntu), Arial Bold (Windows), else PIL's small built-in font. Results are cached (8 sizes).

Draws lines of white text on a half-transparent dark box in the top-left (default) or bottom-left corner of a picture. The text height is 1/30 of the picture height (18 px on a 960 x 540 stream) so it stays readable when Mission Planner shrinks the picture into its HUD; a grey picture is turned into colour first.

Measures the box (left, top, right, bottom) in pixels that a text takes when drawn at (0, 0). It asks Pillow's draw.textbbox first; when that refuses (Ubuntu 22.04's Pillow 9.0 raises ValueError for its built-in bitmap font), it falls back to the font's older getsize(), so the overlay and the 'waiting for the camera' picture also work there and on a PC without the DejaVu font.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By draw_overlay for every overlay line and by placeholder_jpeg for its one text.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Makes a dark grey 640 x 360 JPEG with the text 'waiting for the camera ...', served while no real picture has arrived (Gazebo still starting).
3x3 rotation matrix for turning by an angle (radians) around the x axis.
3x3 rotation matrix for turning by an angle (radians) around the y axis.
3x3 rotation matrix for turning by an angle (radians) around the z axis (with 0 it is the 'no rotation' matrix).
Multiplies two 3x3 matrices (chains two rotations).
Rotation matrix of an (x, y, z, w) quaternion, normalised first; a zero quaternion gives 'level' (no rotation).

Works out (yaw, pitch, roll) in degrees the way the SIYI camera reports them, from the three gimbal joint angles (radians) and the drone's world orientation (None = a level drone). It chains drone body -> yaw joint (+Z) -> roll joint (+X) -> pitch joint (-Y) and then splits the camera's direction in the gimbal's own motor order (yaw -> roll -> pitch, like siyi_emulator's gimbal_earth_angles): pitch against the HORIZON (-90 = straight down, + = up, and smoothly on past -90, e.g. -90.4), roll + = right side down, yaw = the yaw joint (against the nose, + = left). This split stays steady while the camera looks straight down (the earlier split gave a random roll there) and is only undefined at roll +-90 deg, far outside the gimbal's range.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By GimbalReadout.lines for line 1 of the overlay.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Formats an angle with one decimal and never shows '-0.0'.

Keeps the newest measured gimbal joints and drone attitude and turns them into the overlay text (no ROS inside; the node feeds it). Joint names are matched by their last part after '::' or '/' (gimbal_yaw, gimbal_roll, gimbal_pitch from the sim_models drone), so scoped names work too.
Stores the clock (monotonic seconds; a fake one in tests), the staleness limit (2 s) and the joint names, with no data yet.
Takes one JointState (names + positions in radians) and stores the yaw, roll and pitch joint angles with the time, but only when all three are present and finite. Returns True when they were.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: For every /sim/gimbal/joint_states message (about 50 per second).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Stores the drone's world orientation quaternion with the time; a zero or non-finite quaternion is ignored (returns False).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: For every /sim/drone/odometry message.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The overlay text: 'gimbal pitch -90.0 deg, yaw 0.0 deg, roll 0.0 deg' (+ '(drone attitude unknown: level drone assumed)' when the attitude is missing or older than 2 s) and 'joints (vs drone): pitch ..., yaw ..., roll ... deg'; or one line 'gimbal: no angle data yet' / 'gimbal: no angle data for N s' when the joints are missing or stale.
Holds the newest JPEG, shared between the ROS callback (the writer) and the HTTP threads (the readers), with a sequence number and a condition variable so streams can wait for the next picture.
Starts empty (no picture, sequence 0) with a clock and a threading Condition.
Stores a new newest picture, increases the sequence number, records the time and wakes every waiting stream.
Returns (sequence number, newest JPEG or None).
Waits up to timeout_s for a picture newer than the given sequence number and returns the newest one either way (so a quiet camera still gets its last picture repeated).
Seconds since the newest picture arrived, or None before the first one (shown on /health).
How many pictures have been stored so far.

Builds the small HTML help page served at '/': the live picture and the three clicks for Mission Planner (right-click the HUD, Video > Set MJPEG Source, paste <url>/pov.mjpg), plus links to /pov.jpg and /health; light and dark colours.

A small threaded HTTP server that serves the pictures of a FrameStore, at most 8 viewers at once, repeating the newest picture every 1 s while the camera is quiet so a viewer never sees a dead connection.
Stores the frame store, host (127.0.0.1), port (8081), keep-alive time (1 s) and maximum viewers (8); nothing listens yet.
The address viewers use, e.g. 'http://127.0.0.1:8081' (loopback is shown when listening on every address).

Starts listening on a background thread (a request-handler class bound to this server is made on the fly) and returns itself. If the port is taken it raises OSError with a plain hint ('Another program (an earlier camera feed?) may be using the port ... -p port:=8082').
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Opens a TCP listening socket on host:port (default 127.0.0.1:8081).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: A one-line subclass of _Handler created inside start() so every request knows which PovServer it belongs to (its server_owner).
Stops listening, closes the socket and waits up to 5 s for the server thread; safe to call twice.
The grey 'waiting for the camera' JPEG, made once and reused.
Reserves a viewer slot for a new stream; False when 8 viewers are already watching.
Gives a viewer slot back when a stream ends.
How many streams are open right now (shown on /health as viewers).
Handles one HTTP request (HTTP/1.0, so a stream simply ends when the connection closes).
Does nothing, to keep the console quiet (a stream would otherwise log every connection).
Sends one complete answer with a status code, content type, length and 'Cache-Control: no-store'.

Routes a GET request: /pov.mjpg -> the stream, /pov.jpg -> the newest picture (or the placeholder), /health -> 'ok frames=N newest_age_s=X viewers=N', / or /index.html -> the help page, anything else -> 404. A viewer closing the window is ignored quietly.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the HTTP server thread for every browser or Mission Planner request.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Sends pictures as multipart/x-mixed-replace (boundary 'astraframe') until the viewer goes away: waits up to 1 s for a newer picture and sends it, or repeats the newest (or the placeholder). Answers 503 'too many viewers' when all 8 slots are taken.

Entry point of 'ros2 run sim_demo pov_server': declares the parameters (topic /sim/camera/image, host 127.0.0.1, port 8081, max_fps 10, quality 75, max_width 960, overlay true, overlay_position top_left, gimbal_topic /sim/gimbal/joint_states, odometry_topic /sim/drone/odometry), starts the PovServer (exits with an error if the port is taken), subscribes to the camera (BEST_EFFORT, depth 1) and, with the overlay on, to the gimbal joints and drone odometry, logs the Mission Planner instructions and spins until Ctrl+C.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8081; subscriptions /sim/camera/image, /sim/gimbal/joint_states, /sim/drone/odometry.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Runs for each /sim/camera/image message: skips it if the last encoded picture was less than 1/max_fps seconds ago, otherwise encodes it (with the current gimbal overlay) and puts it in the FrameStore. A bad picture is counted and skipped, with a warning at most every 30 s, never raised.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.explain: START OVER: brings a running simulator back to the START of the search mission so it can be flown again, without closing any window (Gazebo, RViz and the demo panel stay open). It runs 14 numbered steps, 15 with --fly: check (find the running simulator in state/current_launch.yaml + its session tag), handover (stop the previous run's watchers), stop_team (stop ./launcher.sh sim and the team nodes), land (RTL or LAND and wait for disarm), archive (move old photos into the OLD run folder), remove (delete the drone entity 'iris' from Gazebo WHILE SITL STILL RUNS), stop_ap (stop SITL + MAVProxy after recording their command lines), spawn (a fresh drone with both payloads from the same model file), start_ap (SITL + MAVProxy with the same command lines), helpers (new run folder; restart score_run, payload_release, demo_markers, truth_detector), ready (GPS + EKF + pre-arm, ~30-60 s), upload (the survey mission), team (start the team stack like demo.sh), watch (run watcher) and fly (only with --fly: arm + AUTO). The order matters: ardupilot_gazebo runs in lock-step with SITL, so stopping SITL first would freeze Gazebo.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_.how_it_fits: Called by simulation/scripts/start_over.sh (terminal and Windows 'Start Over.bat') and the demo panel's START OVER button (through demo_panel.StartOverLink). It writes progress to stdout and as JSON lines to <sim home>/state/start_over_progress.jsonl, which the panel follows. It only stops processes carrying the simulator's ASTRA_SIM_SESSION tag, uses the simulator's own GZ_PARTITION / ROS_DOMAIN_ID for every gz and ros2 command, and talks to Gazebo through the gz command line, to ArduPilot through pymavlink, and to ROS through 'ros2' commands. Status in AGENTS.md: unit-tested, runtime acceptance still pending (WIP). Every outside effect goes through small adapter classes so test/test_run_reset.py checks the whole state machine with fakes.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: How long each wait may take (seconds) before START OVER gives a clear message: land 300, demo_exit 40, stop 20, remove 30, spawn 90, sitl_port 60, ready 360, stack 300.
The error a failed step raises; its message is a plain sentence saying what happened and what to do.
A ResetError meaning no simulator is running; start_over.sh then starts a fresh demo instead (exit code 3).
The simulator's state folder: $ASTRA_SIM_HOME, else ~/.astra_sim (same rule as sim_bringup).
The (x, y, z, w) quaternion of a turn by yaw radians around the vertical axis (used for the spawn pose).
The folder of a new run: <home>/runs/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>_<world>, the same pattern demo.sh uses.

The parts of state/current_launch.yaml (written by sim_bringup's sim.launch.py at start) that START OVER needs: session tag, world and world_name, the generated drone model file, spawn pose, mission, detector, SITL instance, ports, GCS/MAVROS/panel ports (14550/14552/14553), Windows GCS address, SITL run folder, photo folder, home, GZ_PARTITION and ROS_DOMAIN_ID.
UDP port of the Gazebo <-> SITL physics link: the recorded 'fdm' port, else 9002 + 10 x instance.
TCP port of SITL's first MAVLink serial: the recorded 'serial0' port, else 5760 + 10 x instance.
pymavlink URL of MAVProxy's ground-station output inside Linux, e.g. 'udpin:127.0.0.1:14550'.

Reads <home>/state/current_launch.yaml into a SimState (strings, integers, spawn and ports); the session written in state/session by start_sim.sh / demo.sh wins. A missing file raises NotRunning ('No simulator has been started yet'), a broken one ResetError.
One running process as read from /proc: pid, process group, parent pid, command-line words, working folder and environment.
The command line as one string (for matching and messages).
The simulator session tag (ASTRA_SIM_SESSION) the process carries in its environment, '' if none.

Gives a process its role from its command line: start_over / watcher / guard (this module), demo (demo.sh), gz_server or gz_gui ('gz sim -s' / '-g'), sitl (arducopter), mavproxy, team (launcher.sh, team_stack.launch.py, tracker.launch.xml, MAVROS, new_od, siyi, trigger, waypoint, gpstest, main_controller.py, humanize.sh), sim_launch, panel, score_run, markers, truth_detector, payload_release, phase_monitor, mission_tool, stack_check, gz_follow, odom_tf, emulator, bridge, rviz, else 'other'.

Picks the processes of the given session whose role is in the wanted list, never a protected role (gz server/window, panel, RViz, sim launch, bridge, emulator, odom_tf) and never an excluded pid (START OVER itself and its parents). Only the session tag gives permission: a team stack started by hand without the tag is never stopped.
Finds the demo.sh process(es) of the session: demo.sh exports ASTRA_SIM_SESSION only after it started, so it counts when it carries the tag itself OR has at least one tagged child.

The process groups that may get Ctrl+C as a whole: only groups whose EVERY member is a target (like the team stack, which demo.sh starts with setsid). A group containing anything else (for example demo.sh's own group with its phase monitor) is never signalled as a whole, because that would make demo.sh close the whole simulator.
The real process table and signals through Linux /proc and os.kill; the tests use a fake with the same methods.
Lists every process of this user from /proc: pid, process group, parent, argv (cmdline), working folder (cwd link) and environment (environ). Processes that end while being read are skipped.
True while a process exists and is not a zombie (state Z in /proc/<pid>/stat).
Sends a signal to one process, ignoring ones that are already gone or not ours.
Sends a signal to a whole process group.
Starts a program in the background in its OWN session (so it outlives START OVER), with output appended to a log file, and returns its pid.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Starts a process; appends to a log file.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: This process (or a given pid) and all its parents up the tree, so START OVER never stops itself or whoever called it.

Stops processes politely: Ctrl+C (SIGINT) to safe process groups or else to each pid, waits up to 'grace' seconds, then SIGTERM (5 s), then SIGKILL (3 s). Returns the processes still alive (normally none).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Sends signals to processes.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: How to start a program again: argv, working folder and environment (recorded from /proc before it is stopped).
The JSON form saved in state/start_over_specs.json: argv and cwd only (the environment is not saved; it is re-read).
Builds the Spec that restarts a process; if it is still wrapped in sim_bringup's wait_then_exec, only the real program after '--' is kept (START OVER waits for the ports itself).
Adds '-p name:=value' to a ROS 2 node's argv (adding '--ros-args' if needed), replacing an earlier -p for the same name; a later -p wins over the launch's params file.
Removes a '--params-file' whose temporary file (written by the launch into /tmp) is gone, and gives the fallback parameters with -p instead.
Reads a ROS parameter's value from a node's command line: from '-p name:=value', or from its --params-file YAML (ros__parameters); '' if not found.
Lists the local ports that are bound (UDP) or listening (TCP, state 0A) by reading /proc/net/udp(6) or /proc/net/tcp(6), without opening any test connection.

Talks to the Gazebo world through the 'gz' command line tool (it inherits GZ_PARTITION / GZ_IP from the environment): list, remove and spawn models, check the Gazebo window, read one odometry message, and check ports.
Remembers the world name used in Gazebo service names (/world/<name>/...).
Runs 'gz <args>' with a timeout (default 20 s) and returns its output, or None when it failed, timed out or could not start.
Calls a Gazebo world service /world/<world>/<name> with a request type and text, expecting a gz.msgs.Boolean answer; True only when the answer says 'data: true'.
True when 'gz model --list' shows the model (for example 'iris'). If Gazebo does not answer it raises ResetError and the drone is left in place.
Asks Gazebo (service 'remove', gz.msgs.Entity type MODEL) to delete a model; its plugins, sensors and attached payloads go with it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Removes a Gazebo entity.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Asks Gazebo (service 'create', gz.msgs.EntityFactory) to spawn an SDF file as a named entity at (x, y, z) turned by yaw, without renaming (what ros_gz_sim create does at start). 15 s timeout.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Creates a Gazebo entity (the drone 'iris' with both payloads).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: True when the Gazebo WINDOW is open, judged by whether the '/gui/follow' service exists (then the camera can follow the new drone).
Reads ONE gz.msgs.Odometry message from a Gazebo topic (gz topic -e -n 1) and returns its (x, y, z), or None; used to check where the payloads are.
True while some program has the UDP port open (the drone's ArduPilot plugin opens 9002 + 10 x instance).
True while some program listens on the TCP port (SITL: 5760 + 10 x instance).
What the autopilot says right now: armed, mode name, height above home (m) and MAVLink landed state (1 on ground, 2 in air, 3 taking off, 4 landing).
True when the landed state says 'on ground', or when the height is below 1.5 m and the landed state does not say in air / taking off / landing.
A tiny pymavlink client on MAVProxy's ground-station output (opened only for the landing step) that can read the flight state, change mode and disarm.

Connects with system id 246 / component 190 and waits up to 20 s for an ArduPilot HEARTBEAT; otherwise raises ResetError ('No autopilot heartbeat on ... Is MAVProxy running ...?'). pymavlink is imported only here, so the module works and is tested without it.
Listens for 1.5 s and returns a FlightSnapshot from the latest HEARTBEAT (armed flag, mode name), GLOBAL_POSITION_INT (relative altitude) and EXTENDED_SYS_STATE (landed state).
Switches the flight mode (RTL or LAND) and confirms it from the heartbeat, retrying for up to 8 s.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Sends MAVLink set-mode messages to ArduPilot.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Sends MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM to disarm; with force (only on the ground) it adds ArduPilot's magic number 21196.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Sends a MAVLink COMMAND_LONG.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Closes the connection so the UDP port is free again (mission_tool needs it next).
Runs the simulator's own command line tools (mission_tool, stack_check, ros2 ...) and passes each output line on as it comes.

Runs a command to the end, handing every output line to on_line (printed and used as progress details); after the timeout it sends Ctrl+C, waits 10 s and kills it. Returns the exit code (124 = timed out, 127 = could not start).
Real time (monotonic seconds and sleep); the tests use a fake clock that jumps instead of sleeping.
Monotonic seconds.
Waits the given number of seconds.
Checks a condition every 0.5 s (or 'every') until it is true (returns True) or the time is up (returns False).
The progress file the demo panel reads: <home>/state/start_over_progress.jsonl.

Writes START OVER's progress twice: '[start over] ...' lines for the terminal and the same as JSON lines {t, id, kind, step, n, total, text, run_dir} in the progress file for the panel (kind = step, info, ok, warn, error, detail, done or failed).
Stores the progress file path (None = terminal only), the reset id, the number of steps and the print function.

Begins a new progress file by REPLACING the old one (writes an empty '.new' file and renames it), so the panel's ProgressTracker always notices the new start by the file's identity, even if the new file grows past the old size before it looks.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Replaces <home>/state/start_over_progress.jsonl.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Appends one JSON progress line to the file (errors are ignored so progress can never break the reset).
Announces a new step: prints '[start over] ===== STEP 5/15: Archive the old photos and detections' and writes a 'step' line.
Prints and records an info / ok / warn / error line, marked ' OK ', ' !! ' or ' XX '.
Prints a tool's output line indented; at most one per second goes into the file, so the panel is not flooded.
Prints and records the last line: 'DONE: ...' (kind done) or 'FAILED: ...' (kind failed).

Reads the new progress lines from a byte offset and returns (entries, new offset); a file that got shorter than the offset is read from the start, and a half-written last line is kept for the next call.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By ProgressTracker (the demo panel).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: One thing the panel shows, made from one progress line: text, level (colour), step id, kind, new_reset (first line of a NEW start over: clear the old run), finished (True done, False failed, None running) and detail (status line only).

Follows the progress file for the demo panel: which START OVER runs, at which step, and whether it ended. A reset counts as running from its first 'step' line until 'done'/'failed', but at most stale_s (900 s) after its last line, so a reset killed from outside cannot lock the panel's buttons forever. Pure Python, tested with plain files.
Stores the file path, the staleness limit (900 s) and a clock, and starts with offset 0, no file identity, no reset running.
The file's (device, inode) identity and size, or (None, 0) when it does not exist; a new identity means a new START OVER replaced the file.

When a panel starts, loads the current state without replaying history: finished resets stay history, but an unfinished one locks the mission buttons at once, using its recorded time to judge whether it is stale.
True while a START OVER runs: it has not finished and its last line is less than stale_s old.
Reads the lines written since the last call (from the start again if the file was replaced) and turns them into ProgressUpdates, oldest first.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the demo panel every 0.5 s through StartOverLink.poll.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Turns one progress line into one update: a 'step' line starts or continues a reset ('STEP 5/15: ...', new_reset for a new id); lines of the running reset update its time and run folder, and 'done'/'failed' end it ('START OVER done: ...' / 'START OVER FAILED: ...'); lines not belonging to a running reset (like the run watcher's 'Run finished') pass through as plain updates.

Moves every entry of one folder into another (replacing same-named entries, because demo.sh may already have COPIED the same photos there). The source folder itself stays, because video_cam and new_od keep using it. Returns how many entries were moved.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Moves files on disk.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Moves the previous run's team photos (mapping_photos) and new_od's result files (detection_results_sahi) out of the team folders: into the old run folder's photos/ and detections/ when it is known, else into <home>/photo_archive/<stamp>/ (like start_sim.sh). The team photo folder is left empty but present. Returns (where, photos moved, results moved).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Moves files out of <ros2_ws>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos and detection_results_sahi.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: What the user asked for (start_over.sh options): fly (arm + AUTO at the end), world, mission file, land 'land' (straight down, quickest) or 'rtl', team_stack (restart it, default yes), detector ('' = what the simulator uses) and the run watcher's timeout (120 min).

Runs the START OVER steps in order (step_check ... step_fly). Every outside effect goes through the adapters it is given (ProcessOps, GzOps factory, MavlinkOps factory, CommandOps, Clock, Progress), so the tests replace them with fakes.

Stores the options and adapters (real ones by default), a copy of the environment, the pids never to touch (itself and its parents), a time stamp, the step list (without 'fly' unless --fly) and a Progress writer on the panel's progress file; the simulator state, mission, old/new run folders, recorded SITL/MAVProxy specs and the team stack's TRACKER_CMD/FCU_URL are filled in by the steps.
Writes a progress line (info / ok / warn / error).
The current process table from the ProcessOps adapter.
The processes of the simulator's session with the given roles (through select, never protected roles or excluded pids).
