Stops the session's processes with the given roles (Ctrl+C, then TERM, then KILL) and says 'stopping the <what> (N processes)'; raises ResetError naming what is still running. Returns how many there were.
Runs 'ros2 run sim_bringup <args>' (mission_tool, stack_check, gz_follow ...) with a timeout, showing its lines as progress details.
Starts a recorded program (Spec) in the background with the simulator's ASTRA_SIM_SESSION tag (so stop_sim.sh finds it) plus any extra environment, logging into the new run folder (or <home>/logs).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Starts a process.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Runs every step under a one-at-a-time lock. Whatever happens, the progress file gets a last 'done' or 'failed' line (the panel waits for it to unlock its buttons) and only then is the lock released. Ends with 'ready to fly again. Press UPLOAD MISSION + START ...' or 'the drone is flying the mission again', and returns 0 (done), 1 (a step failed), 3 (no simulator running) or 130 (Ctrl+C: run START OVER again to finish).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By main for 'python3 -m sim_demo.run_reset reset' (start_over.sh).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Releases and closes the lock file (state/start_over.lock).

Claims <home>/state/start_over.lock with a non-blocking file lock before touching anything; if another START OVER holds it, raises 'Another START OVER is already running ...' without touching the running reset's progress file.

Step 1: loads the simulator state and session, checks the Gazebo server of that session still runs (else NotRunning), adopts the simulator's GZ_PARTITION / ROS_DOMAIN_ID, refuses if an untagged team stack uses the same ROS domain, if another world or detector was asked for, or if the drone model file or mission file is missing. Then it finds the old run folder and the mission, creates the new run folder with start_over.env, writes state/keep_open (so a still-running demo.sh leaves everything open) and opens the GzOps.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Creates <home>/runs/<stamp>_<world>/start_over.env and <home>/state/keep_open.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Makes START OVER talk to the simulator in ITS Gazebo partition and ROS domain (recorded by sim.launch.py), even from a terminal with other settings; otherwise 'gz service' would ask another (or no) Gazebo and the restarted team stack would not see the simulator's topics.

Finds the folder of the run that is ending: the last START OVER's (state/current_run.json for this session), else score_run's run_dir parameter or ASTRA_RUN_DIR, else any session process's ASTRA_RUN_DIR, else '' (started with start_sim.sh).
The mission file a run flew, read from MISSION= in its start_over.env or demo.env ('' if not recorded).

Step 2: stops the previous run's watchers (phase_monitor, mission_tool, stack_check, an older run watcher), waits up to 40 s for demo.sh to finish the previous run politely (score report, photos) and makes sure the old run has its score report.

If the old run folder has no score_report.md yet and score_run still runs, calls 'ros2 service call /sim/demo/write_score std_srvs/srv/Trigger' (25 s timeout) so the previous run gets its report before the recorder is restarted.

Step 3: stops the team flight stack (launcher.sh, MAVROS, video_cam, new_od, trigger, waypoint_manager, main_controller) so nothing fights the landing or writes photos. It first saves launcher.sh's TRACKER_CMD and FCU_URL for the restart, and also stops any other program in the process groups the team stack leads (for example a plug-in detector). If demo.sh recorded the stack as 'external' it only says to restart it there.
Reads state/team_stack.env written by demo.sh (TRACKER_CMD, FCU_URL, STACK_CHECK_ARGS, TEAM_STACK_WHERE) if its SESSION is this simulator's; {} otherwise.

Step 4: if the drone entity still exists, connects to the autopilot through MAVProxy's GCS port. On the ground and disarmed it does nothing; armed on the ground it force-disarms; flying, it commands LAND (or RTL with --land rtl, LAND as a fallback) and waits up to 300 s for 'LANDED and disarmed', reporting the height every 10 s. Without MAVProxy or a working link it refuses and leaves the drone in place (safety: no removal without a verified landing).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: MAVLink mode change / disarm to ArduPilot.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Step 5: moves the old photos and detector results into the old run folder (or a photo archive) with archive_photos, so the team photo folder is empty again (old photos would be detected again and could send the drone to old targets).

Before anything is stopped, records how SITL and MAVProxy were started: from the running processes, else from state/start_over_specs.json, else rebuilt from the simulator's settings; then saves them in start_over_specs.json.

Only when no record exists: builds the SITL command (arducopter --model JSON -I <instance> --home <home> --defaults ...astra_sitl.parm ...) or the MAVProxy command (--master tcp:127.0.0.1:5760+10I, --out udp 14550 / 14552 / 14553 [+ Windows GCS], --daemon) with sim_bringup.sim_paths.

Step 6: records the autopilot commands, then removes the drone 'iris' from Gazebo WHILE SITL STILL RUNS (lock-step: without SITL Gazebo is frozen; if SITL is missing it starts a temporary one). It waits up to 30 s until the model is gone and the physics port (UDP 9002 + 10 x instance) is free.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Removes the Gazebo entity 'iris' (its payloads go with it).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Step 7: stops MAVProxy and ArduCopter SITL of the session (5 s grace) and waits up to 15 s until SITL's TCP port (5760 + 10 x instance) is free.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Stops the SITL and MAVProxy processes.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Step 8: asks Gazebo to spawn a fresh drone 'iris' from the SAME generated model file at the world's spawn pose, waits up to 90 s until its ArduPilot plugin opens UDP 9002 + 10 x instance, then checks that both payloads (/sim/payload/person|tent/odometry) are within 0.5 m of the drone (/sim/drone/odometry), i.e. attached.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Creates the Gazebo entity 'iris' with both payloads.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Step 9: starts SITL again with its recorded command line, waits up to 60 s for its TCP port, starts MAVProxy with its recorded command line (same outputs 14550 / 14552 / 14553 and Windows GCS), checks it stays up, and starts the session guard.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Starts the arducopter and mavproxy.py processes (logs sitl.log, mavproxy.log in the new run folder).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Starts one 'python3 -m sim_demo.run_reset guard --session <id>' per session (if none runs yet): when the Gazebo server ends, the guard stops the processes START OVER started, so nothing is left behind.

Step 10: restarts the per-run helper nodes with fresh memories: score_run (pointed at the NEW run folder with -p run_dir:=), payload_release, demo_markers and truth_detector (if used); missing temporary params files are replaced by -p world / photo_dir / detector. If the Gazebo window is open it starts gz_follow so the camera follows the new drone, and it writes state/current_run.json.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Stops and restarts helper processes (ASTRA_RUN_DIR = new run folder); writes <home>/state/current_run.json.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Step 11: runs 'ros2 run sim_bringup mission_tool --url udpin:127.0.0.1:14550 --timeout 360 wait-ready' and waits until the new autopilot has a GPS fix, a healthy EKF and passed its pre-arm checks (normally 30-60 s).
Step 12: uploads the survey mission with 'mission_tool --url ... upload --mission <file>' (like Mission Planner's Write WPs).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: MAVLink mission upload to ArduPilot (through mission_tool).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The environment for './launcher.sh sim': the same TRACKER_CMD and FCU_URL as before (from the old launcher.sh or demo.sh's record), else demo.sh's defaults 'ros2 launch sim_bringup team_stack.launch.py detector:=<d>' and FCU_URL tcp://127.0.0.1:5763+10I (SITL SERIAL2, wired like the Jetson on TELEM2), plus ASTRA_SIM_SESSION and ASTRA_RUN_DIR.
The options for sim_bringup's stack_check: the ones demo.sh recorded (for example a plug-in's --skip-node), else --need-detector for the real detector.

Step 13: starts the team flight stack exactly like demo.sh ('cd $ASTRA_REPO && ./launcher.sh sim' with TRACKER_CMD / FCU_URL in its own session, log team_stack.log), waits with 'stack_check --settle 20' until MAVROS is connected, the mission read, the detector loaded and the nodes stayed up 20 s, restarts it once if not, and finally points the camera down by publishing 'gimbal_set_angles 0,-90' on /camera/command. Skipped with --no-team-stack or when the stack runs elsewhere.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Starts launcher.sh (MAVROS + the team's tracker.launch.xml nodes); publishes once on /camera/command.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Step 14: starts the run watcher in the background ('python3 -m sim_demo.run_reset watch-run --run-dir <new run> --photo-dir <team folder>'), which records the phases and collects photos and the score report after the landing.
Step 15 (only with --fly): 'mission_tool --url ... fly' arms and starts AUTO, and confirms the take-off.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: MAVLink arm + AUTO (through mission_tool).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: After the landing: waits up to 30 s for score_run's score_report.md (it is written about 8 s after landing), otherwise asks for it with /sim/demo/write_score, then COPIES the team photos and new_od's result files into the run folder's photos/ and detections/ (the team folder keeps them so the panel can still show them; the next START OVER moves them away). Returns plain log lines.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Copies files into the run folder; may call the /sim/demo/write_score service.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The run watcher: runs sim_bringup's phase_monitor (log phases.jsonl, timeout in minutes) until the drone has landed, then collect_run, and writes 'Run finished (the drone has landed). ...' to the progress file (the panel shows it). If a new START OVER stops it (SIGINT/SIGTERM are forwarded to phase_monitor) it still collects but writes no 'finished' line.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By 'python3 -m sim_demo.run_reset watch-run' (started by step_watch).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Signal handler of the run watcher: remembers that a stop was asked and passes Ctrl+C on to the phase_monitor child.

Waits (checking every 2 s) while the session's Gazebo server is alive; when it is gone, stops the session processes still running (the SITL, MAVProxy, team stack and helpers a START OVER started, which are not children of the simulator's launch, so its Ctrl+C would not reach them).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By 'python3 -m sim_demo.run_reset guard --session ID' (started by start_guard).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: The Windows name of a Linux file (wslpath -w, e.g. \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-22.04\home\...), or '' outside WSL.

The same mission file in the Windows copy of the repo (<ASTRA_WINDOWS_REPO>\ros2_ws\src\simulation\sim_worlds\missions\<file>), when the Windows folder is known (set by the simulation/windows/*.bat launchers); else ''.

Builds the competition procedure in Mission Planner as numbered plain lines: 1 CONNECT (UDP, port 14550 or the Windows GCS port), 2 MISSION (PLAN > Load File > the mission file's Windows path > Write), 3 WAIT ~30 s for the autopilot to settle, 4 ARM, 5 AUTO within 10 s, 6 WATCH; plus how to run it again with START OVER.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By 'python3 -m sim_demo.run_reset mp-steps' (printed by demo.sh --manual and start_over.sh).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Finds simulation/scripts/start_over.sh of the repo the simulator runs from: $ASTRA_REPO first, then up to 8 folders above this file (a --symlink-install build links it into the repo); None if not found.

Starts a START OVER in the background, detached from the caller (own session, output to <home>/logs/start_over_<stamp>_panel.log): 'bash start_over.sh <args>', or if the script is not found 'python3 -m sim_demo.run_reset reset' (without --no-fresh). Returns (pid, log path).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By the demo panel's StartOverLink.launch (second START OVER click).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.effects: Starts start_over.sh as a detached process; creates the log file.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.explain: Command line 'python3 -m sim_demo.run_reset <command>': reset [--fly] [--world W] [--mission FILE] [--land land|rtl] [--land-timeout S] [--no-team-stack] [--detector real|truth] [--watch-timeout-min M] runs the Resetter; watch-run --run-dir DIR [--photo-dir DIR] [--timeout-min M] runs the run watcher; guard --session ID runs the guard; mp-steps [--mission FILE] [--windows-gcs ADDR] prints the Mission Planner steps; plan prints the 15 steps and changes nothing. Returns the exit code (0 done, 1 failed, 2 bad usage, 3 no simulator, 130 Ctrl+C).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/sim_d.called_when: By simulation/scripts/start_over.sh and by the processes START OVER starts for itself.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: Pure pytest, no ROS.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: Pure pytest; never touches Windows.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: Pure pytest, no ROS or Gazebo.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.explain: Unit tests of truth_model.py and photo_geometry.py: a target under the camera is found at the picture centre with a sensible confidence, an offset hiker appears right and up when heading north, targets outside the picture or too small are not reported, zoom shrinks what is visible, results are repeatable and depend on the seed, detect_probability 0 reports nothing, the confidence curve's shape, pose_from_sample using height and heading, and PhotoGeometry end to end.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: Pure pytest, no ROS.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.explain: Unit tests of the tolerant world/truth loader world_info.py: the fixture world in the contract's format, class aliases (mannequin/hiker -> person), keyed targets and pose lists, a document keyed by name, polygon formats, the exact sim_worlds schema (trimmed copy of truth/runway.yaml), config search areas with radian yaw, a missing world raising and a missing truth file only warning.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: Pure pytest, no ROS.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.explain: End-to-end driver that plays a complete ~90 s search mission over a test world WITHOUT Gazebo or SITL: it publishes what MAVROS would (/mavros/state, global_position/global + rel_alt + compass_hdg, vfr_hud, mission/reached, statustext/recv) and what the team's nodes would say on /mavros/statustext/send ('Camera trigger STARTED', 'Targets: tent@9 -> person@10. Diverting.', 'Servo 13 -> 1400' ...), a live camera picture on /sim/camera/image rendered from a painted world, and a 2560x1440 photo every second (emulator /sim/camera/photo_info record first, then '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' written like video_cam). It records what the sim_demo nodes publish back and checks it, using the team's own main_controller callback (team_acceptance.py).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: ROS 2 test program, run by run_fake_mission_e2e.sh (not part of the plain pytest suite).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.explain: Bash end-to-end test of the four sim_demo nodes against the scripted fake mission: starts truth_detector, demo_markers, score_run (run_dir in the output folder, linger 4 s, no Gazebo payload tracking) and demo_panel (offscreen, 6 screenshots, mission_link mavros) on the fixture world with ROS_DOMAIN_ID 47, plays fake_mission.py (~90 s), keeps a few hit photos, and prints E2E_RESULT=PASS when the fake mission succeeded, the report says 'Targets found: 2 of 2' and screenshots exist. Usage: bash run_fake_mission_e2e.sh OUTPUT_DIR [photo_info:1|0].
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: Needs a sourced ROS 2 Humble workspace with sim_demo and interfaces built, numpy and Pillow.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.explain: A tiny pretend 'simulator' for the e2e test: paints a top-down picture of a world (grass with mowing stripes, a runway, bushes, and the tent and mannequin from the answer key at their true positions and sizes) and renders what a camera at any pose would see with sim_demo's own camera model. Because the pictures and truth_detector use the same geometry, the stand-in's boxes must land exactly on the painted targets.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: Used by fake_mission.py; numpy + Pillow only.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.explain: Proves that what truth_detector publishes is accepted by the TEAM'S OWN mission controller code: it loads main/src/main_controller.py read-only and runs its real MainController.image_result_cb on each /image_detection message with a tiny stand-in for 'self' (building the real node would block waiting for MAVROS services); best() then tells what main_controller would fly to. Only wp_sender.parameter is stubbed when that package is not built.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: Used by fake_mission.py.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.explain: A small fake world config in the contract's format (home '38.315400,-76.549000,10.0,0', spawn, mission and truth file names), used only by the unit tests (world 'testfield').

Fake answer key for the unit tests that deliberately mixes position styles (metres x/y for the hiker, GPS lat/lon for the tent) and class names ('mannequin', type 'tent'), plus a 'boulder' that must be skipped with a warning, and a square search area.
A small QGC WPL 110 test mission: home, TAKEOFF to 30 m, DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL, six survey waypoints and RETURN_TO_LAUNCH (10 items).

A trimmed copy of sim_worlds/config/runway.yaml in exactly sim_worlds' schema (home '36.2143000,-96.0068000,210.0,0', spawn yaw 1.5708, a 120 x 100 m search_box), so the loader is tested against the real format without building sim_worlds.

A trimmed copy of sim_worlds/truth/runway.yaml (made by build_runway.py, seed 7) in the exact sim_worlds schema: targets and distractors with id/class/x/y/z/yaw (radians)/lat/lon/size/center/center_z, and search_areas with corners_xy / corners_latlon.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.explain: The test folder of sim_demo: 20 test_*.py files plus conftest.py, panel_fakes.py and render_panel_preview.py (draws the panel offscreen with fakes), small fixture worlds in fixtures/, and ros_e2e/, a separate fake-mission end-to-end check with ROS (run_fake_mission_e2e.sh, fake_mission.py, synthetic_world.py, team_acceptance.py). The unit tests replace Windows, the process table, Gazebo, the autopilot and the clock with fakes, so they never start a simulator, signal a real process or open Mission Planner. Some skip themselves when an optional piece is missing: the panel tests need PyQt5 and rclpy, the ImageResult round trip needs the built interfaces and vision_msgs packages, and one mission test needs pymavlink.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_demo/test.how_it_fits: AGENTS.md runs it from the package folder with 'QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 -m pytest -q test --ignore=test/ros_e2e'; the ros_e2e folder needs a built workspace with ROS 2 and is run on its own. Each file has one module-level entry in this map, not one per test.
